sources: ابن خلكان، وفيات الأعيان، ج3 ص271
الذهبي، سير أعلام النبلاء، ج18 ص420

en.title: Death of Imam al-Qadi al-Mawardi
en.body: Imam Ali ibn Muhammad al-Mawardi passed away, the judge, Shafi'i jurist, famous legal theorist and eloquent writer. He left great works, among them 'al-Hawi al-Kabir', 'A'lam al-Nubuwwa' and his Tafsir. He was a just judge, a skilled jurist and an eloquent writer, and he left a vast scholarly legacy.

sources: الذهبي، سير أعلام النبلاء، ج21 ص166
ابن خلكان، وفيات الأعيان، ج3 ص295

en.title: Death of Imam al-Hafiz Abd al-Ghani al-Maqdisi
en.body: Imam Abd al-Ghani ibn Abd al-Wahid al-Maqdisi passed away, the great hadith master, Hanbali jurist and virtuous scholar. He was known for his vast memorization of hadith and the religious sciences. He wrote beneficial books on hadith and jurisprudence, and was a refuge for students of knowledge in his time.

sources: ابن الأثير الكامل في التاريخ
المقريزي السلوك لمعرفة دول الملوك

en.title: The conquest of Acre and the end of the Crusader presence on the Levantine coast
en.body: Sultan al-Ashraf Khalil ibn Qalawun conquered the city of Acre, the last Crusader stronghold in the Levant. This conquest ended the military presence of the Crusaders in the Levant for good after two centuries of wars.

sources: الذهبي سير أعلام النبلاء
ابن خلكان وفيات الأعيان

en.title: Death of Imam al-Tirmidhi
en.body: Abu Isa Muhammad ibn Isa al-Tirmidhi, author of al-Jami, passed away in Tirmidh in 279 AH. He was among the great hadith scholars and authors of the Sunan collections.

sources: المؤرخون العثمانيون (تاريخ ابن الأثير والمقريزي)
الموسوعات التاريخية الحديثة

en.title: The conquest of Constantinople by Sultan Mehmed the Conqueror
en.body: The Ottoman Sultan Mehmed the Conqueror (Muhammad al-Fatih) conquered Constantinople, the capital of the Byzantine Empire, after a siege that lasted 53 days. It marked the end of a Byzantine state that had lasted a thousand years and was a great Islamic conquest.

sources: الموسوعة السعودية الرسمية
موقع وزارة الشؤون الإسلامية السعودية

en.title: Proclamation of the unification of Saudi Arabia
en.body: King Abdulaziz ibn Abd al-Rahman Al Saud proclaimed the unification of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia under one banner after a long period of successive conquests. A new phase of stability and building began.

sources: المقريزي خطط المقريزية
الذهبي تاريخ الإسلام

en.title: Construction of al-Azhar Mosque in Cairo begins
en.body: The commander Jawhar al-Siqilli, by order of the Fatimid Caliph al-Mu'izz li-Din Allah, began building al-Azhar Mosque in the city of Cairo, which he had recently founded. Al-Azhar later became one of the greatest institutions of Islamic learning throughout history.

sources: الذهبي سير أعلام النبلاء
ابن خلكان وفيات الأعيان

en.title: Death of Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj
en.body: Abu al-Husayn Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj passed away, author of Sahih Muslim, one of the most authentic books after al-Bukhari. He was among the greatest hadith scholars.

sources: الطبري تاريخ الرسل والملوك
ابن الأثير الكامل في التاريخ

en.title: The Battle of the Camel
en.body: The Battle of the Camel took place in Basra between the army of the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib and the forces of the Mother of the Believers Aisha together with al-Zubayr and Talha. It was among the first major internal strifes (fitan) in Islam.

sources: الذهبي سير أعلام النبلاء تاريخ الإسلام
ابن خلكان وفيات الأعيان

en.title: Death of Imam Abu Hamid al-Ghazali
en.body: Abu Hamid Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Ghazali, the Proof of Islam (Hujjat al-Islam), passed away in Tus. He left a great legacy in jurisprudence, Sufism and Islamic philosophy. He is the author of the famous book Ihya Ulum al-Din (The Revival of the Religious Sciences).

sources: الطبري تاريخ الرسل والملوك
ابن سعد الطبقات الكبرى

en.title: Death of the Caliph Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him)
en.body: The first Caliph of the Muslims, Abu Bakr Abdullah ibn Uthman al-Siddiq, passed into the mercy of Allah the Exalted after a caliphate that lasted two years, three months and some days. He left a legacy rich in justice and wisdom.

sources: ابن كثير، البداية والنهاية، الجزء الثالث عشر، سنة 680، ترجمة تقي الدين بن رزين: (توفي ليلة الأحد ثالث رجب منها، ودفن بالمقطم) — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/البداية_والنهاية/الجزء_الثالث_عشر/ثم_دخلت_سنة_ثمانين_وستمائة_من_الهجرة

الذهبي، العبر في خبر من غبر، الجزء الثالث، سنة 680، ترجمة ابن رزين: (ثم ولي قضاء القضاة فلم يأخذ عليه رزقا تدينا وورعا ... توفي في ثالث رجب) — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/العبر_في_خبر_من_غبر/الجزء_الثالث

en.title: Death of the Chief Judge Taqi al-Din Ibn Razin
en.body: In Cairo in 680 AH, the Chief Judge Taqi al-Din Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Razin al-Hamawi al-Shafi'i passed away, a student of Ibn al-Salah. He had issued fatwas in Damascus as a young man, taught at the al-Madrasa al-Shamiyya and led prayer at Dar al-Hadith, then moved to Egypt, where he taught at al-Zahiriyya and held the office of Chief Judge. Al-Dhahabi mentioned that, out of scrupulousness, he took no salary for serving as judge, and that a number of imams studied jurisprudence under him. Ibn Kathir and al-Dhahabi dated his death to the 3rd of Rajab, and he was buried on the slope of al-Muqattam.

sources: عبد الباسط الملطي، نيل الأمل في ذيل الدول، ج2 ص320: (وفي رجب في ثالثه مات الزركشي، الشيخ، العالم، بدر الدين محمد بن بهادر المنهاجي، الشافعي) — https://app.turath.io/book/17097?page=738
ابن قاضي شهبة، طبقات الشافعية 3/167 (بإحالة محقق فتح القريب المجيب، ج1 ص61): (وتوفي في ثالث رجب سنة أربع وتسعين وسبعمائة بالقاهرة) — https://app.turath.io/book/660?page=61

en.title: Death of Imam Badr al-Din al-Zarkashi, author of al-Burhan fi Ulum al-Quran
en.body: In Cairo in 794 AH, Imam Badr al-Din Muhammad ibn Bahadur ibn Abdullah al-Zarkashi passed away, the Shafi'i jurist, legal theorist and hadith scholar, a student of Jamal al-Din al-Isnawi and Ibn Kathir. He combined teaching, issuing fatwas and writing, and left many works in various disciplines, the most famous being al-Burhan fi Ulum al-Quran, al-Bahr al-Muhit in the principles of jurisprudence, al-Manthur fi al-Qawa'id, and al-Tanqih li-Alfaz al-Jami al-Sahih. Abd al-Basit al-Malati and Ibn Qadi Shuhba mentioned that his death was on the 3rd of Rajab.

sources: الذهبي، سير أعلام النبلاء، ج19 ص465 (ط الرسالة)، ترجمة الحريري: (توفي الحريري في سادس رجب سنة ست عشرة وخمس مائة بالبصرة) — https://app.turath.io/book/10906?page=12161
الصفدي، الوافي بالوفيات، ج24 ص98: (توفي في سادس شهر رجب سنة ست عشرة [وخمسمائة]) — https://app.turath.io/book/6677?page=6468
السبكي، طبقات الشافعية الكبرى، ج7 ص269: (توفي في يوم الاثنين ثامن رجب سنة ست عشرة وخمسمائة) — https://app.turath.io/book/6739?page=2584

en.title: Death of al-Hariri, author of the Maqamat, in Basra
en.body: In Basra in 516 AH, the man of letters Abu Muhammad al-Qasim ibn Ali al-Hariri passed away, author of the fifty Maqamat, which became among the most famous works of artistic prose in Arabic, and which scholars passed down through commentary and memorization for centuries. He also wrote Mulhat al-I'rab on grammar and Durrat al-Ghawwas fi Awham al-Khawass. Al-Dhahabi and al-Safadi mentioned that his death was on the 6th of Rajab, while al-Sam'ani and Taj al-Din al-Subki reported that it was on Monday the 8th of Rajab of the same year, when he was about seventy years old.

sources: الطبري، تاريخ الرسل والملوك، الجزء العاشر، سنة 287: (ولسبع خلون من رجب من هذه السنة توفيت ابنة خمارويه بن أحمد بن طولون، زوجة المعتضد) — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/تاريخ_الطبري/الجزء_العاشر

ابن كثير، البداية والنهاية، الجزء الحادي عشر، سنة 287، نقلًا عن ابن الجوزي: (قال ابن الجوزي: لسبع خلون من رجب منها، ودفنت داخل القصر بالرصافة) — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/البداية_والنهاية/الجزء_الحادي_عشر/ثم_دخلت_سنة_سبع_وثمانين_ومائتين

en.title: Death of Qatr al-Nada bint Khumarawayh, wife of the Caliph al-Mu'tadid
en.body: In Rajab 287 AH, Qatr al-Nada bint Khumarawayh ibn Ahmad ibn Tulun, the emir of Egypt, passed away in Baghdad. She was the wife of the Abbasid Caliph al-Mu'tadid Billah, a young woman described as possessing intelligence and beauty. Her marriage was among the most famous events of her era: she was sent from Egypt to Baghdad with an enormous trousseau that became proverbial in the history books, and the marriage was a symbol of reconciliation between the Tulunid state and the Abbasid caliphate. Al-Tabari and Ibn al-Jawzi mentioned that she died on the 7th of Rajab and was buried in the palace of al-Rusafa.

sources: أبو العرب التميمي، طبقات علماء إفريقية، ج1 ص102: (توفي يوم الثلاثاء لسبعة أيام مضت من رجب سنة أربعين ومائتين) — https://app.turath.io/book/13079?page=97
أبو بكر المالكي، رياض النفوس، ج1 ص347: (رجب لسبعة أيام مضت منه قبل صلاة الظهر سنة أربعين ومائتين) — https://app.turath.io/book/148883?page=379

en.title: Death of Imam Sahnun, author of al-Mudawwana, in Kairouan
en.body: In Kairouan in 240 AH, Imam Abu Sa'id Abd al-Salam ibn Sa'id al-Tanukhi, known as Sahnun, passed away, the jurist of the Maghrib and judge of Ifriqiya, through whom the school of Imam Malik spread in the Maghrib. He travelled to Egypt and learned from Ibn al-Qasim and Ashhab, then compiled al-Mudawwana, which became the main reference of the Malikis. In his judgeship he was known for scrupulousness and firmness and for refusing payment for serving as judge. Abu al-Arab al-Tamimi, Abu Bakr al-Maliki and Ibn Yunus mentioned that he died on Tuesday the 7th of Rajab, while al-Qadi Iyad reported another view that it was on the 3rd.

sources: ابن كثير، البداية والنهاية، الجزء الرابع عشر، سنة 705: (وفي يوم الاثنين ثامن رجب حضر القضاة والعلماء، وفيهم الشيخ تقي الدين بن تيمية عند نائب السلطنة بالقصر) — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/البداية_والنهاية/الجزء_الرابع_عشر/ثم_دخلت_سنة_خمس_وسبعمائة

ابن عبد الهادي، العقود الدرية من مناقب شيخ الإسلام ابن تيمية: (وذلك يوم الاثنين ثامن رجب من سنة خمس وسبعمائة طلب القضاة والفقهاء وطلب الشيخ تقي الدين إلى القصر) — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/العقود_الدرية_من_مناقب_شيخ_الإسلام_أحمد_بن_تيمية/7

en.title: Ibn Taymiyya's debate session on al-Aqida al-Wasitiyya in Damascus
en.body: In Rajab 705 AH, the Sultan's deputy in Damascus convened a session in the palace attended by judges and jurists, and Shaykh al-Islam Taqi al-Din Ibn Taymiyya was summoned to be questioned about his creed. He brought his treatise known as al-Aqida al-Wasitiyya, which was read and its issues discussed over more than one session. Ibn Kathir and Ibn Abd al-Hadi dated this session to Monday the 8th of Rajab, and Ibn Taymiyya himself recorded an account of it. These debates are counted among the most famous events of his scholarly life, and the sources have preserved their details and the discussions among the scholars.

sources: الذهبي، تذكرة الحفاظ، الطبقة الثانية عشرة، ترجمة الماسرجسي: (مولده سنة ثمانٍ وتسعين ومائتين، وتوفي في تاسع رجب سنة خمس وستين وثلاثمائة) — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/تذكرة_الحفاظ/الطبقة_الثانية_عشرة

en.title: Death of al-Hafiz al-Masarjisi, author of the largest annotated Musnad
en.body: In Nishapur in 365 AH, the hadith master Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Masarjisi passed away, one of the great hadith scholars of Khurasan. He had travelled and heard hadith from his grandfather, Ibn Khuzayma and Abu al-Abbas al-Sarraj. He compiled a large, refined Musnad with analysis of hidden defects ('ilal) in about one thousand three hundred parts, of which al-Hakim said that no larger Musnad had been compiled in Islam. He gathered the hadith of al-Zuhri in a way no one had done before him, and compiled supplementary collections (mustakhraj) on the Sahihs of al-Bukhari and Muslim. Al-Dhahabi and al-Suyuti mentioned that his death was on the 9th of Rajab.

sources: ابن كثير، البداية والنهاية، الجزء الثالث عشر، سنة 680، وقعة حمص: (لما كان يوم الخميس رابع عشر رجب التقى الجمعان وتواجه الخصمان عند طلوع الشمس) — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/البداية_والنهاية/الجزء_الثالث_عشر/ثم_دخلت_سنة_ثمانين_وستمائة_من_الهجرة

الذهبي، العبر في خبر من غبر، الجزء الثالث، سنة 680: (وفي يوم الخميس رابع عشر رجب كانت وقعة حمص. أقبل منكوتمر بن هولاوو بجيوش أخيه أبغا) — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/العبر_في_خبر_من_غبر/الجزء_الثالث

en.title: The Second Battle of Homs and the Mamluk victory over the Mongols
en.body: In Rajab 680 AH, the Mongol army under Mengu-Timur son of Hulagu advanced on the Levant in great numbers. Sultan al-Mansur Qalawun went out to meet them with the armies of Egypt and the Levant, and the two sides met near Homs on Thursday the 14th of Rajab. The fighting intensified until the Mongols were broken and withdrew from the Levant. This was among the most important battles protecting the Levant, two decades after Ayn Jalut, and Ibn Kathir and al-Dhahabi dated it to this day.

sources: ابن الأثير، أسد الغابة، ترجمة معاوية بن أبي سفيان: (وتوفي معاوية النصف من رجب سنة ستين) — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/أسد_الغابة_(ط._الوهبية)/حرف_الميم/باب_الميم_والعين/معاوية

en.title: Death of Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan (may Allah be pleased with them both) in Damascus
en.body: In Rajab 60 AH, the Companion Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan (may Allah be pleased with them both) passed away in Damascus, a scribe of the Revelation and founder of the Umayyad state, after about twenty years as caliph and twenty years before that as governor of the Levant. In his reign the conquests expanded in North Africa and the lands of the Byzantines, and he had established the first large Islamic navy while governor of the Levant. Historians differed on the day of his death: Ibn al-Athir and others mentioned it was in the middle of Rajab, while Ibn Ishaq and others narrated it was eight days before the end of the month, and Ibn Kathir reported all the views.

sources: الطبري، تاريخ الرسل والملوك، الجزء التاسع، حوادث سنة 256: (خلع المهتدي، وتوفي يوم الخميس لاثنتي عشرة ليلة بقيت من رجب) — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/تاريخ_الطبري/الجزء_التاسع

en.title: Death of the Abbasid Caliph al-Muhtadi Billah
en.body: In Rajab 256 AH, the Abbasid Caliph Muhammad ibn al-Wathiq, titled al-Muhtadi Billah, died in Samarra after the Turkish army commanders deposed him following a dispute with them; his caliphate did not complete a single year. Al-Muhtadi was known among the Abbasid caliphs for asceticism, scrupulousness, devotion to justice and abundant worship, so that some historians likened him to Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz. The well-known view in al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir is that he died on Thursday with twelve nights remaining in Rajab, and Ibn Kathir reported another narration placing his death two days earlier.

sources: الذهبي، العبر في خبر من غبر، الجزء الثالث، سنة 635، ترجمة الكامل: (مرض بقلعة دمشق بالسعال والإسهال نيفا وعشرين ليلة ... فمات في الحادي والعشرين من رجب) — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/العبر_في_خبر_من_غبر/الجزء_الثالث

ابن كثير، البداية والنهاية، الجزء الثالث عشر، سنة 635: (وكانت وفاته في ليلة الخميس الثاني والعشرين من رجب من هذه السنة) — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/البداية_والنهاية/الجزء_الثالث_عشر/ثم_دخلت_سنة_خمس_وثلاثين_وستمائة

en.title: Death of Sultan al-Kamil al-Ayyubi, liberator of Damietta
en.body: In Rajab 635 AH, Sultan al-Malik al-Kamil Nasir al-Din Muhammad ibn al-Adil al-Ayyubi, ruler of Egypt, passed away in the Citadel of Damascus after a short illness, having taken Damascus two months before his death. He ruled Egypt for about forty years, first as his father's deputy and then as sultan. He was known for honouring scholars and sitting with them, and was renowned for his steadfastness against the Fifth Crusade until he recovered Damietta after a long siege. Al-Dhahabi mentioned that he died on the 21st of Rajab, while Ibn Kathir placed it on the eve of Thursday the 22nd.

sources: الطبري، تاريخ الرسل والملوك، الجزء الخامس، سنة 60: (وكان مخرج الحسين من المدينة إلى مكة يوم الأحد لليلتين بقيتا من رجب سنة ستين) — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/تاريخ_الطبري/الجزء_الخامس

ابن كثير، البداية والنهاية، الجزء الثامن، قصة الحسين بن علي وسبب خروجه من مكة: (وكان خروج الحسين من المدينة إلى مكة يوم الأحد لليلتين بقيتا من رجب سنة ستين) — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/البداية_والنهاية/الجزء_الثامن

en.title: Al-Husayn ibn Ali (may Allah be pleased with them both) leaves Madinah for Makkah
en.body: In late Rajab 60 AH, al-Husayn ibn Ali (may Allah be pleased with them both) left Madinah heading for Makkah with his family, after he was asked to pledge allegiance to Yazid ibn Mu'awiya and declined. Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir mentioned that he departed on Sunday with two nights remaining in Rajab, and entered Makkah on the eve of Friday the 3rd of Sha'ban, staying there for the rest of Sha'ban, Ramadan, Shawwal and Dhu al-Qa'dah. This journey was the beginning of the march that ended in the tragedy of Karbala in Muharram of the following year.

sources: الطبري، تاريخ الرسل والملوك، الجزء التاسع، سنة 255: (وفي يوم الأربعاء لليلة بقيت من رجب من هذه السنة، بويع محمد بن الواثق؛ فسمي المهتدي بالله) — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/تاريخ_الطبري/الجزء_التاسع

ابن كثير، البداية والنهاية، الجزء الحادي عشر، سنة 255: (كانت بيعته يوم الأربعاء لليلة بقيت من رجب من هذه السنة) — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/البداية_والنهاية/الجزء_الحادي_عشر/ثم_دخلت_سنة_خمس_وخمسين_ومائتين
ابن عبد ربه، العقد الفريد، الجزء الرابع: (بويع المهتدي ... يوم الأربعاء لليلة بقيت من رجب سنة خمس وخمسين ومائتين)

en.title: Allegiance to al-Muhtadi Billah as caliph in Samarra
en.body: In late Rajab 255 AH, Muhammad ibn al-Wathiq received the pledge of allegiance as caliph in Samarra and was titled al-Muhtadi Billah, after al-Mu'tazz abdicated before judges and witnesses. Al-Muhtadi was among the most ascetic and devout of the Abbasid caliphs; he strove to establish justice, sat to hear grievances and reduced the palace's expenses, but his caliphate lasted less than a year. The sources agree that the pledge to him was on Wednesday with one night remaining in Rajab.

sources: الذهبي، تذكرة الحفاظ، الطبقة 17 — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/تذكرة_الحفاظ/الطبقة_السابعة_عشرة

en.title: Death of al-Hafiz Ali ibn al-Mufaddal al-Maqdisi in Cairo
en.body: At the beginning of Sha'ban 611 AH, the hadith master Sharaf al-Din Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn al-Mufaddal al-Maqdisi, later al-Iskandarani, passed away in Cairo, one of the great hadith scholars of Egypt in the Ayyubid era. He studied under al-Hafiz Abu Tahir al-Silafi in Alexandria and served as deputy judge there, then moved to Cairo and taught at the madrasa of al-Sahib Ibn Shukr. Among his most famous students was al-Hafiz Zaki al-Din al-Mundhiri, author of al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib, so he was an important link in transmitting the science of hadith between two generations of Egyptian scholars. He was buried on the slope of al-Muqattam.

en.title: Al-Husayn ibn Ali (may Allah be pleased with them both) enters Makkah
en.body: On the eve of Friday the 3rd of Sha'ban 60 AH, al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with them both) entered Makkah coming from Madinah, having left it in late Rajab following the death of Mu'awiya (may Allah be pleased with him). He stayed in Makkah for the rest of Sha'ban, Ramadan, Shawwal and Dhu al-Qa'dah, with people gathering around him and visitors seeking him out, until he left for Iraq on the Day of Tarwiyah. This stay in Makkah is an important chapter of his life (may Allah be pleased with him) in his final months.

en.title: Caliph al-Mustansir Billah invests al-Zahir Baybars with the sultanate
en.body: On Monday the 4th of Sha'ban 659 AH, a great ceremony was held outside Cairo in an enormous tent, attended by the Abbasid Caliph al-Mustansir Billah, the judges, the emirs and the people of authority. The Caliph invested Sultan al-Zahir Baybars with the rule of the lands, clothed him in the black robe of the caliphate, and his diploma of investiture was read to the people. This came after al-Mustansir had received allegiance as caliph in Cairo following the fall of Baghdad to the Mongols. The event heralded the revival of the Abbasid caliphate in Egypt and its continuation as a unifying symbol for Muslims for nearly two and a half centuries.

en.title: Birth of al-Husayn ibn Ali (may Allah be pleased with them both)
en.body: On the 5th of Sha'ban 4 AH, al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with them both) was born in Madinah, the grandson of the Prophet ﷺ and his sweet basil, and his mother was Fatima al-Zahra (may Allah be pleased with her). He was born about a year after his brother al-Hasan (may Allah be pleased with him), and the Prophet ﷺ performed tahnik for him and named him. He grew up in the house of Prophethood, narrated from his grandfather ﷺ and from his parents, and was renowned for worship, generosity and courage. This date is what al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar and others narrated, and some historians hold other views on the day of his birth.

en.title: Death of Ibn al-Najjar, historian of Baghdad
en.body: On the 5th of Sha'ban 643 AH, the hadith master Muhibb al-Din Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Mahmud Ibn al-Najjar al-Baghdadi passed away in Baghdad, one of the great historians of the East. He travelled widely in pursuit of knowledge to the Levant, Egypt, the Hijaz, Isfahan and Khurasan, and compiled 'Dhayl Tarikh Baghdad' as a continuation of al-Khatib al-Baghdadi's book, along with works on narrators, the history of Madinah and the virtues of al-Shafi'i. He bequeathed his books as an endowment (waqf) to the Nizamiyya madrasa so that students of knowledge after him could benefit from them.

en.title: Death of the ascetic Abu al-Qasim al-Qabbari in Alexandria
en.body: On the 6th of Sha'ban 662 AH, the righteous Shaykh Abu al-Qasim Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Qabbari passed away in Alexandria at the age of seventy-five, one of the famous ascetics of Egypt in the Mamluk era. He lived in a small orchard which he worked with his own hands, living on its fruits and feeding people from them, and he was known for intense scrupulousness and care in seeking what is lawful. He enjoined good and forbade evil and admonished the governors, who listened to him because of his asceticism. Nasir al-Din Ibn al-Munayyir devoted a separate work to his biography.

en.title: Death of al-Hafiz Abu Khaythama Zuhayr ibn Harb
en.body: On the eve of Thursday the 7th of Sha'ban 234 AH, the hadith master Abu Khaythama Zuhayr ibn Harb al-Nasa'i passed away in Baghdad, one of the trustworthy imams of hadith. He heard hadith from Hushaym, Sufyan ibn Uyayna and their generation, and al-Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud and others narrated from him; Imam Muslim narrated from him extensively in his Sahih. Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi described him as trustworthy, reliable, a hadith master and meticulous. He was a peer of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal and Yahya ibn Ma'in in Baghdad.

en.title: Death of al-Hafiz Zayn al-Din al-Iraqi
en.body: On the 8th of Sha'ban 806 AH, the hadith master Zayn al-Din Abu al-Fadl Abd al-Rahim ibn al-Husayn al-Iraqi passed away in Cairo, the hadith master of his era and shaykh of the hadith scholars in Egypt. He revived the tradition of hadith dictation after it had lapsed, and composed 'Alfiyyat al-Hadith' on the sciences of hadith terminology together with its commentary, and 'al-Mughni an Haml al-Asfar' tracing the hadiths of the Ihya. Among his most prominent students were al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani and al-Hafiz Nur al-Din al-Haythami, and he had a profound influence on the revival of hadith scholarship in the ninth century AH.

en.title: The Battle of Alarcos (al-Arak) in al-Andalus
en.body: On Wednesday the 9th of Sha'ban 591 AH, the Almohad army led by the Caliph Abu Yusuf Ya'qub al-Mansur, together with the troops of al-Andalus, the tribes of the Maghrib and volunteers, met the army of Alfonso VIII, King of Castile, at the fortress of Alarcos south of Toledo. The battle ended in a great victory for the Muslims and the withdrawal of the King of Castile. Alarcos was counted as the greatest Almohad victory in al-Andalus; it delayed the advance of the northern Spanish kingdoms by about two decades, and its spoils were invested in buildings in Marrakesh and Rabat al-Fath.

en.title: Death of the Chief Judge Abu Bakr al-Shami in Baghdad
en.body: On Tuesday the 10th of Sha'ban 488 AH, the Chief Judge Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Muzaffar ibn Bakran al-Hamawi al-Shafi'i, known as al-Shami, passed away in Baghdad at the age of eighty-eight. He studied jurisprudence under al-Qadi Abu al-Tayyib al-Tabari and taught steadily in his mosque for more than fifty years, then the Caliph al-Muqtadi appointed him Chief Judge. He was renowned for extreme integrity: he took no pay for serving as judge, accepted no gifts, and was careful in accepting witnesses, so that it was said that if the Shafi'i school were lost, he could dictate it from memory.

en.title: Death of Ibn Sayyid al-Nas, author of 'Uyun al-Athar'
en.body: On the 11th of Sha'ban 734 AH, the hadith master Fath al-Din Abu al-Fath Muhammad ibn Muhammad Ibn Sayyid al-Nas al-Ya'mari died suddenly in Cairo; he was Andalusian by origin and Egyptian by residence. He was a hadith scholar, man of letters and poet with fine handwriting, and taught hadith at the al-Zahiriyya madrasa. His most famous work is 'Uyun al-Athar fi Funun al-Maghazi wa al-Shama'il wa al-Siyar', one of the most reliable and widely circulated later books of the Prophetic biography. He began a commentary on Jami al-Tirmidhi that al-Hafiz al-Iraqi completed after him.

en.title: Death of Ibn Malik, author of the Alfiyya on grammar
en.body: Imam Jamal al-Din Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Malik al-Ta'i al-Jayyani, the imam of grammar and language in his era, passed away in Damascus in 672 AH. He was born in Jaén in al-Andalus, then travelled to the East, living in Aleppo and then Damascus. He composed 'al-Alfiyya', which became the most famous didactic poem on Arabic grammar and attracted successive commentaries, along with 'al-Tashil' and 'al-Kafiya al-Shafiya'. The best-known view is that he died on the 12th of Sha'ban, while Ibn Kathir mentioned it was on the eve of the 12th of Ramadan.

en.title: Death of the Caliph al-Qa'im bi-Amr Allah and allegiance to his grandson al-Muqtadi
en.body: On the eve of Thursday the 13th of Sha'ban 467 AH, the Abbasid Caliph al-Qa'im bi-Amr Allah passed away in Baghdad after a caliphate of about forty-four years and eight months, one of the longest Abbasid caliphates. On the same day his grandson Abdullah ibn Muhammad received the pledge of allegiance as caliph, titled al-Muqtadi bi-Amr Allah; he was about twenty years old. He sat to receive allegiance in the Caliphal Palace, and the viziers, emirs and nobles pledged allegiance to him. Al-Muqtadi's reign was known for stability and for choosing judges and viziers from among righteous people.

en.title: Death of Imam Ishaq ibn Rahawayh
en.body: In mid-Sha'ban 238 AH, Imam Abu Ya'qub Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali, known as Ibn Rahawayh, the scholar of Khurasan in his time, passed away in Nishapur. He combined hadith and jurisprudence, was a peer of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and a teacher of al-Bukhari, Muslim and al-Tirmidhi. He was renowned for an astonishing memory, having dictated his 'Musnad' and his Tafsir from memory. His student al-Bukhari dated his death to the eve of the 15th of Sha'ban, while others mentioned it was on the 14th.

en.title: Death of Imam al-Layth ibn Sa'd, the jurist of Egypt
en.body: On Friday in mid-Sha'ban 175 AH, Imam Abu al-Harith al-Layth ibn Sa'd al-Fahmi passed away in Egypt at the age of eighty-one, the jurist and hadith scholar of the Egyptian lands. He narrated from Ata, Nafi, al-Zuhri and others, and was an imam, an authority and trustworthy, so much so that al-Shafi'i said he was more learned in jurisprudence than Malik, except that his companions did not uphold his school. He was known for vast generosity and abundant charity to people of knowledge, and his juristic correspondence with Imam Malik is among the most famous examples of the etiquette of disagreement among scholars.

en.title: Death of Sultan al-Salih Ayyub in al-Mansura during the Crusade
en.body: On the eve of the 15th of Sha'ban 647 AH, the Ayyubid Sultan al-Malik al-Salih Najm al-Din Ayyub passed away in al-Mansura while stationed against the Seventh Crusade led by King Louis IX of France, which had seized Damietta. His wife Shajar al-Durr concealed news of his death and continued issuing orders in his name until his son Turan Shah arrived from Hisn Kayfa, in order to preserve the army's cohesion. Months later the campaign ended with the defeat of the Crusaders and the capture of their king at Fariskur, and al-Salih's death was a prelude to the rise of the Mamluk state in Egypt.

en.title: The fire at the Great Umayyad Mosque in Damascus
en.body: On the eve of the 15th of Sha'ban 461 AH, a huge fire broke out at the Umayyad Mosque in Damascus. It began in the governor's residence known as al-Khadra, adjoining the mosque on the qibla side, following a fight between quarrelling soldiers, then spread to the mosque: its gilded ceilings collapsed and its famous mosaics, which had covered its walls with scenes of cities, trees and rivers, were scattered. The mosque had been built in the reign of al-Walid ibn Abd al-Malik and was counted among the wonders of Islamic architecture; much of its original decoration was lost in this fire, and it was rebuilt in later eras.

en.title: Death of the encyclopedic scholar Kamal al-Din Ibn Yunus al-Mawsili
en.body: In mid-Sha'ban 639 AH, the erudite scholar Kamal al-Din Abu al-Fath Musa ibn Yunus ibn Man'a al-Mawsili, the shaykh of the Shafi'is in his city, passed away in Mosul at about eighty-eight years of age. He studied jurisprudence under his father and then at the Nizamiyya madrasa in Baghdad, and read grammar with Kamal al-Din al-Anbari. He then excelled in the rational sciences and mathematics, so that it was said he mastered fourteen disciplines, and he was unique in his time in his mastery of mathematics. Students travelled to him from many lands, and he taught at several madrasas in Mosul.

en.title: Death of al-Hafiz Ibn Nasir, the hadith scholar of Iraq
en.body: In Sha'ban 550 AH, the hadith master Abu al-Fadl Muhammad ibn Nasir al-Salami al-Baghdadi, the hadith scholar of Iraq in his time, passed away in Baghdad at the age of eighty-three, and was buried at Bab Harb. He first excelled in language and literature, then devoted himself to hadith, and moved from the school of al-Shafi'i to that of Ahmad. He was trustworthy, reliable and abstinent; he endowed his books and left nothing behind but worn-out clothes and a few dinars. Among his most famous students was Imam Ibn al-Jawzi. Ibn Kathir, and al-Dhahabi in al-Ibar, dated his death to the 18th of Sha'ban, while al-Dhahabi mentioned in al-Tadhkira that it was on the 12th.

en.title: Deposition of the Caliph al-Ta'i li-Allah and allegiance to al-Qadir Billah
en.body: On Saturday the 19th of Sha'ban 381 AH, the Buyid Sultan Baha al-Dawla deposed the Abbasid Caliph al-Ta'i li-Allah in Baghdad. After the Caliph had sat in his usual assembly, he was carried off to the royal palace and his abdication was witnessed. A letter was written to his cousin Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Ishaq ibn al-Muqtadir, who was living in al-Bata'ih; he came to Baghdad in Ramadan and took the title al-Qadir Billah. This event is evidence of the weakness of the caliphate before the Buyid sultans, yet al-Qadir ruled for forty-one years and restored some of the caliphate's prestige.

en.title: Birth of the Abbasid Caliph al-Wathiq Billah
en.body: On Monday the 20th of Sha'ban 196 AH, Harun ibn Muhammad al-Mu'tasim ibn Harun al-Rashid was born, who later became the ninth Abbasid caliph with the title al-Wathiq Billah; his mother was a Byzantine umm walad named Qaratis. He assumed the caliphate by designation from his father al-Mu'tasim in 227 AH. He was a man of letters who loved knowledge, poetry and singing, and in his reign the Mihna (inquisition) over the doctrine of the createdness of the Quran continued. He died in Samarra in 232 AH and was succeeded by his brother al-Mutawakkil, who ended the Mihna.

en.title: The fall of Jerusalem to the Crusaders
en.body: In the forenoon of Friday the 23rd of Sha'ban 492 AH, the army of the First Crusade stormed Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis) after a siege lasting about a month and a half. The city fell and a large number of its inhabitants were killed; it was among the most terrible calamities to befall the Muslims in that era. Its fall caused widespread shock in the Muslim world, and al-Masjid al-Aqsa remained under Crusader control for about ninety-one Hijri years, until Salah al-Din al-Ayyubi recovered it in 583 AH.

en.title: Death of al-Hafiz Mughultay, author of 'al-Zahr al-Basim'
en.body: On Tuesday the 24th of Sha'ban 762 AH, the hadith master Ala al-Din Mughultay ibn Qilij al-Bakjari al-Hanafi passed away in Cairo, one of the great hadith masters of Egypt. He took over teaching hadith at the al-Zahiriyya madrasa after Ibn Sayyid al-Nas, and had wide knowledge of genealogies and narrators. His works exceeded one hundred, among them a commentary on Sahih al-Bukhari, a supplement to Tahdhib al-Kamal, and 'al-Zahr al-Basim fi Sirat Abi al-Qasim' ﷺ. He remained devoted to reading and writing until the end of his life.

en.title: Al-Afshin's victory over the Byzantine Emperor at the Battle of Anzen
en.body: On Thursday the 25th of Sha'ban 223 AH, the commander al-Afshin, at the head of one of the armies of the Abbasid Caliph al-Mu'tasim, met the army of the Byzantine Emperor Theophilos in Anatolia. Al-Afshin held firm after a difficult round, and the encounter ended with the Emperor's withdrawal and the dispersal of his troops. This encounter was part of al-Mu'tasim's great campaign in response to the Byzantine raid on Zibatra, and it paved the way for the Abbasid army's advance towards Ankara and then Amorium.

en.title: Death of Imam al-Suhayli, author of 'al-Rawd al-Unuf'
en.body: On the 25th of Sha'ban 581 AH, Imam Abu al-Qasim Abd al-Rahman ibn Abdullah al-Suhayli al-Andalusi, scholar of language, hadith and the Prophetic biography, passed away in Marrakesh. He was born near Malaga and lost his sight at the age of seventeen, but that did not prevent him from mastering the sciences. His most famous work is 'al-Rawd al-Unuf', a commentary on Ibn Hisham's biography of the Prophet, one of the most precious commentaries on the Sira. The Almohad sultan summoned him to Marrakesh and honoured him, and he served there as chief judge until his death. Ibn Kathir dated his death to the 26th of Sha'ban.

en.title: Birth of Imam Ibn Daqiq al-Id
en.body: On Saturday the 25th of Sha'ban 625 AH, Taqi al-Din Abu al-Fath Muhammad ibn Ali al-Qushayri, known as Ibn Daqiq al-Id, was born on the coast of Yanbu in the Hijaz while his parents were on their way to Hajj. He grew up in Upper Egypt and excelled in both Maliki and Shafi'i jurisprudence as well as hadith and usul, until he was regarded as the renewer (mujaddid) of his age, and he held the office of Chief Judge of Egypt. Among his works are 'Ihkam al-Ahkam Sharh Umdat al-Ahkam' and 'al-Ilmam bi-Ahadith al-Ahkam'.

en.title: Death of Yazid ibn Abd al-Malik and Hisham's accession to the caliphate
en.body: With four days remaining in Sha'ban 105 AH, the Umayyad Caliph Yazid ibn Abd al-Malik passed away after a caliphate of about four years and was buried in al-Balqa in the Levant. His brother Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik received the pledge of allegiance as caliph by Yazid's designation, at the age of thirty-four. Hisham's caliphate lasted about twenty years, one of the longest of the Umayyads; he was known for resolve, good management and orderly administration, and his reign saw expansion on the frontiers and great building activity.

en.title: Death of the hadith scholar Abu Nu'aym al-Fadl ibn Dukayn
en.body: On the last day of Sha'ban 219 AH, the hadith master Abu Nu'aym al-Fadl ibn Dukayn al-Mula'i passed away in Kufa, one of the eminent trustworthy hadith scholars and a teacher of al-Bukhari. He heard hadith from al-A'mash, Sufyan al-Thawri, Mis'ar and their generation, and was a marvel of precision, so much so that Yahya al-Qattan said he did not care who contradicted him if Abu Nu'aym agreed with him. Most historians mention that he was buried on the last day of Sha'ban, while some said his death was in Ramadan.

en.title: Death of al-Imad al-Katib al-Asfahani, historian of Salah al-Din
en.body: At the beginning of Ramadan 597 AH, Imad al-Din Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Katib al-Asfahani passed away in Damascus, one of the leading figures of chancery prose and literature in the sixth century AH. He served Nur al-Din Mahmud Zangi and then Salah al-Din al-Ayyubi in the chancery, and witnessed the conquests with him, recording their history in 'al-Fath al-Qussi fi al-Fath al-Qudsi' about the recovery of Jerusalem and in 'al-Barq al-Shami', and he collected the poets of his era in 'Kharidat al-Qasr'. His books are considered a primary source for the history of the Ayyubid state. He was buried in the Sufi cemetery.

en.title: The Battle of Shaqhab (Marj al-Suffar) and the defeat of the Tatars
en.body: On Saturday the 2nd of Ramadan 702 AH, the Mamluk army led by Sultan al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun, accompanied by the Abbasid Caliph and the troops of Egypt and the Levant, met the invading Tatar army at Shaqhab near Damascus. The fighting raged from the afternoon until the morning of the following day; then the Tatars were defeated and scattered in the wilderness, and many of them drowned in the Euphrates. Imam Ibn Taymiyya was among those who urged people to stand firm, and the Sultan entered Damascus on the 5th of Ramadan amid general rejoicing.

en.title: Al-Ma'mun appoints Ali al-Rida as heir apparent
en.body: On Tuesday the 2nd of Ramadan 201 AH, the Abbasid Caliph al-Ma'mun, while in Merv, gave the pledge of succession to Ali ibn Musa al-Kazim ibn Ja'far al-Sadiq as his heir, titling him 'al-Rida min Al Muhammad' (the one approved from the family of Muhammad). He ordered that black, the emblem of the Abbasids, be abandoned in favour of green, and wrote of this to all regions. Historians mention that al-Ma'mun looked among the Abbasids and the descendants of Ali and found none more excellent in knowledge and piety. The decision provoked objection from a group of Abbasids in Baghdad, and Ali al-Rida died in Tus in 203 AH before assuming rule.

sources: الطبري، تاريخ الرسل والملوك، الجزء الثالث (سنة 11، عن الواقدي) — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/تاريخ_الطبري/الجزء_الثالث

en.title: Death of Fatima al-Zahra (may Allah be pleased with her)
en.body: On the eve of Tuesday the 3rd of Ramadan 11 AH, Fatima al-Zahra, daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (may Allah be pleased with her), passed away in Madinah, a few months after the death of her father ﷺ, at about twenty-nine years of age. She is the leader of the women of the people of Paradise, the mother of al-Hasan and al-Husayn (may Allah be pleased with them both), and the wife of Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him). She was the youngest of his daughters ﷺ and the most beloved of them to him. She was buried at night in al-Baqi, and historians hold other views on how long she lived after the Prophet ﷺ.

en.title: Death of Abd al-Malik ibn Habib, jurist of al-Andalus
en.body: On the 4th of Ramadan 238 AH, Abd al-Malik ibn Habib al-Sulami, the mufti and scholar of al-Andalus, passed away in Cordoba at about seventy-four years of age. He travelled to the East and learned from the companions of Imam Malik in Madinah and Egypt, then returned and spread the Maliki school in al-Andalus, until leadership in knowledge there passed to him after Yahya ibn Yahya al-Laythi. Among his most famous works is 'al-Wadiha' in jurisprudence, one of the earliest foundational books of the Malikis, and he also wrote a book of history. Other years have also been given for his death.

en.title: Death of al-Hafiz Abu Musa Abdullah ibn Abd al-Ghani al-Maqdisi
en.body: On Friday the 5th of Ramadan 629 AH, the hadith master Abu Musa Abdullah, son of al-Hafiz Abd al-Ghani al-Maqdisi, author of 'Umdat al-Ahkam', passed away in Damascus. He travelled in pursuit of hadith to Isfahan, Nishapur, Mosul, Irbil and the Two Holy Sanctuaries, studied jurisprudence under Shaykh Muwaffaq al-Din Ibn Qudama, and read Arabic with Abu al-Baqa al-Ukbari. Ibn al-Hajib said of him that there was no one like him in his era in memorization, knowledge and trustworthiness, and his assemblies of admonition and hadith in Damascus became famous.

en.title: Al-Mu'tasim lays siege to Amorium
en.body: On Friday the 6th of Ramadan 223 AH, the Abbasid Caliph al-Mu'tasim Billah descended with his army on the city of Amorium in the heart of Anatolia, his commander Ashinas having preceded him there by a day; he surrounded it and began the siege. The campaign was a response to the Byzantine Emperor's raid on the city of Zibatra and what befell its people. The siege ended with the conquest of the city, and the poet Abu Tammam immortalized this conquest in his famous poem rhyming in 'ba': 'The sword is truer in tidings than books.'

en.title: Death of Ibn Bashkuwal, historian of the scholars of al-Andalus
en.body: On the 8th of Ramadan 578 AH, the hadith master Abu al-Qasim Khalaf ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Bashkuwal al-Ansari, the hadith scholar and historian of al-Andalus, passed away in Cordoba at the age of eighty-four. He heard from the great shaykhs of Cordoba and Seville, received a license (ijaza) from Abu Ali al-Sadafi, and served as deputy judge in some districts of Seville. His most famous book is 'al-Sila', with which he continued Ibn al-Faradi's history of the scholars of al-Andalus, and which became a primary reference for the biographies of Andalusian scholars, along with 'Ghawamid al-Asma al-Mubhama'.

en.title: The Prophet ﷺ leaves Madinah for the Conquest of Makkah
en.body: On the 10th of Ramadan 8 AH, the Prophet ﷺ left Madinah with about ten thousand of the Muhajirun, the Ansar and the Arab tribes, heading for Makkah after Quraysh had broken the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah by aiding Banu Bakr against Khuza'a, the allies of the Muslims. He appointed Abu Ruhm Kulthum ibn Husayn al-Ghifari (may Allah be pleased with him) over Madinah, and concealed his destination so that Quraysh would not prepare. He travelled while fasting until he reached al-Kadid, then camped at Marr al-Zahran. This was the prelude to the Conquest of Makkah, which took place days later.

en.title: Assassination of the vizier Nizam al-Mulk, founder of the Nizamiyya madrasas
en.body: On the 10th of Ramadan 485 AH, the Seljuk vizier Nizam al-Mulk al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Tusi was assassinated near Nahavand while travelling with Sultan Malikshah to Baghdad; he was stabbed by a man of the Batiniyya who approached him in the guise of a petitioner with a grievance. Nizam al-Mulk had managed the affairs of the Seljuk state for about thirty years and was renowned for patronizing knowledge and its people. He founded the Nizamiyya madrasas in Baghdad, Nishapur and elsewhere, whose teachers included Abu Ishaq al-Shirazi, al-Juwayni and al-Ghazali.

en.title: Death of Imam Ibn al-Jawzi in Baghdad
en.body: In Ramadan 597 AH, Imam Abu al-Faraj Abd al-Rahman ibn Ali Ibn al-Jawzi passed away in Baghdad, the preacher of his era and one of the most prolific authors in Islamic history. He wrote 'Zad al-Masir' in exegesis, 'al-Muntazam' in history, and 'Sayd al-Khatir' and other works on admonition and matters that soften the heart. His preaching assemblies were attended by caliphs, viziers and tens of thousands. His bier was carried on people's heads and he was buried at Bab Harb near Imam Ahmad. Al-Dhahabi and al-Suyuti dated his death to Friday the 13th, while Ibn Kathir mentioned the eve of Friday the 12th.

en.title: Death of al-Hafiz Zaki al-Din al-Birzali al-Ishbili
en.body: On the eve of the 14th of Ramadan 636 AH, the hadith master Zaki al-Din Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Birzali al-Ishbili, the travelling hadith scholar of the Levant, passed away in Hama. He came from al-Andalus for Hajj in 602 AH and devoted himself to hearing hadith, travelling to Makkah, Damascus, Isfahan, Nishapur, Herat, Merv, Baghdad and Mosul. He wrote a great deal, compiled 'al-Mu'jam al-Kabir' of his teachers, and compiled collections for many scholars. He settled in Damascus as imam of the Fulus Mosque, and was known for humility and for giving books freely to students of knowledge.

en.title: Death of the jurist Kamal al-Din Ibn al-Zamlakani
en.body: At dawn on Wednesday the 16th of Ramadan 727 AH, the erudite scholar Kamal al-Din Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abd al-Wahid al-Ansari, known as Ibn al-Zamlakani, one of the great Shafi'i jurists of Damascus, passed away in the town of Bilbays on his way to Cairo. He was born in 667 AH, studied jurisprudence under Taj al-Din al-Fazari, headed Dar al-Hadith al-Ashrafiyya and taught at several madrasas, then became judge of Aleppo; he was summoned to be appointed judge of Damascus, but death overtook him. He had a quick mind and was skilled in debate, and wrote works on jurisprudence and usul. He was buried in al-Qarafa near the dome of al-Shafi'i.

en.title: Death of the Mother of the Believers Aisha bint Abi Bakr (may Allah be pleased with her)
en.body: On the eve of Tuesday the 17th of Ramadan, the Mother of the Believers Aisha bint Abi Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with them both), wife of the Prophet ﷺ, passed away in Madinah. She was the foremost female jurist of the Ummah and the most prolific of its women in narrating hadith, and senior Companions would refer to her on matters of knowledge. She asked to be buried at night in al-Baqi; Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him) led the funeral prayer over her, and members of her family descended into her grave. The well-known view is that she died in 58 AH, and it is also said 57 AH, when she was nearly sixty-seven years old.

sources: الذهبي، تذكرة الحفاظ، الطبقة 13 — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/تذكرة_الحفاظ/الطبقة_الثالثة_عشرة

en.title: Death of al-Hafiz Abu Ali al-Kashshi al-Shirazi
en.body: On the 18th of Ramadan 405 AH, the imam, hadith master and jurist Abu Ali al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Layth al-Kashshi, later al-Shirazi, passed away in Shiraz, one of the great imams of Persia in hadith and the Quranic readings. He travelled to Baghdad and Nishapur and heard from Isma'il al-Saffar, Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm, Ibn al-Akhram and others. Al-Hakim al-Naysaburi praised him, describing him as advanced in knowledge of the readings, a hadith master and a great traveller. He had students among the hadith masters who spread his knowledge in Persia, and Ibn al-Salah mentioned him in Tabaqat al-Shafi'iyya.

en.title: Death of the historian Abu Shama al-Maqdisi
en.body: On the 19th of Ramadan 665 AH, Imam Shihab al-Din Abu al-Qasim Abd al-Rahman ibn Isma'il al-Maqdisi, known as Abu Shama, the Quran reciter, grammarian and historian, passed away in Damascus. He excelled in the Quranic readings and wrote a commentary on 'al-Shatibiyya' on the seven readings, abridged Ibn Asakir's 'History of Damascus', and headed the teaching of recitation at al-Turba al-Ashrafiyya and Dar al-Hadith al-Ashrafiyya. His most famous book is 'al-Rawdatayn fi Akhbar al-Dawlatayn al-Nuriyya wa al-Salahiyya', a principal source for the history of Nur al-Din and Salah al-Din.

sources: الطبري، تاريخ الرسل والملوك، الجزء التاسع (سنة 222)، ذكر خبر فتح البذ — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/تاريخ_الطبري/الجزء_التاسع

en.title: The conquest of al-Badhdh, stronghold of Babak al-Khurrami
en.body: On Friday the 20th of Ramadan 222 AH, the commander al-Afshin, leader of the armies of the Abbasid Caliph al-Mu'tasim, conquered the city of al-Badhdh in Azerbaijan, the fortified stronghold of Babak al-Khurrami, who had led a widespread rebellion lasting about twenty years that exhausted the caliphate's armies. The conquest came after a long siege and fierce battles, and al-Mu'tasim reinforced the army with money and men. Babak fled after the fall of his fortress and was captured in the same year, thus ending one of the most dangerous upheavals of the early Abbasid era.

sources: ابن كثير، البداية والنهاية، ج11 سنة 273 — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/البداية_والنهاية/الجزء_الحادي_عشر/ثم_دخلت_سنة_ثلاث_وسبعين_ومائتين
الذهبي، تذكرة الحفاظ، الطبقة 10 — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/تذكرة_الحفاظ/الطبقة_العاشرة

en.title: Death of Imam Ibn Majah, author of the Sunan
en.body: On the 22nd of Ramadan 273 AH, Imam Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Majah al-Qazwini passed away in Qazvin at the age of sixty-four. He travelled in pursuit of hadith to Iraq, the Hijaz, the Levant and Egypt, and compiled the 'Sunan', which became one of the six canonical books of Prophetic hadith, along with a Tafsir and a History. Abu Ya'la al-Khalili described him as a great, trustworthy scholar, agreed upon and relied upon as proof. His brother Abu Bakr led the funeral prayer over him, and his two brothers and his son undertook his burial.

en.title: Death of al-Hafiz Ibn Mardawayh al-Asbahani
en.body: On the 24th of Ramadan 410 AH, the hadith master Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Musa ibn Mardawayh, the hadith scholar, exegete and historian of Isfahan, passed away in Isfahan at nearly ninety years of age. He heard hadith in Isfahan and Iraq, and had deep insight into narrators and extensive expertise in this field. He compiled a large exegesis based on transmitted reports, on which later exegetes such as Ibn Kathir and al-Suyuti relied, as well as 'al-Mustakhraj ala Sahih al-Bukhari' and 'Tarikh Asbahan'. He is regarded as one of the most prominent hadith masters of the fourth and fifth centuries AH.

sources: الطبري، تاريخ الرسل والملوك، الجزء الثالث (سنة 8) — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/تاريخ_الطبري/الجزء_الثالث

en.title: Khalid ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) destroys the idol al-Uzza
en.body: On the 25th of Ramadan 8 AH, days after the Conquest of Makkah, the Prophet ﷺ sent Khalid ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) to Batn Nakhla between Makkah and Ta'if, where the house of al-Uzza stood, the greatest idol of Quraysh and Kinana. He destroyed it and returned to inform the Prophet ﷺ. The destruction of al-Uzza was among the expeditions the Prophet ﷺ sent in those days to remove the landmarks of idolatry around Makkah, such as the destruction of Suwa' and Manat, and so the Peninsula was purified of the greatest symbols of polytheism.

sources: الطبري، تاريخ الرسل والملوك، الجزء السابع (سنة 129) — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/تاريخ_الطبري/الجزء_السابع

en.title: The proclamation of the Abbasid call in Khurasan
en.body: On the eve of Thursday the 25th of Ramadan 129 AH, Abu Muslim al-Khurasani openly proclaimed the Abbasid call in the village of Safidhanj near Merv. He raised the two black banners that Ibrahim al-Imam had sent him, and he and his companions wore black, which became the emblem of the new state. He had arrived in Merv at the beginning of Ramadan of the same year, and people flocked to him from the surrounding villages. This proclamation marked the beginning of the revolution that ended the Umayyad state in the East and established the Abbasid caliphate in 132 AH.

en.title: Death of the Shafi'i jurist Ibn Kajj al-Dinawari
en.body: On the eve of the 27th of Ramadan 405 AH, al-Qadi Abu al-Qasim Yusuf ibn Ahmad ibn Kajj, one of the great imams of the Shafi'is and among the authorities whose views count within the school (ashab al-wujuh), was killed in Dinawar by a band of brigands ('ayyarun) during a period of turmoil following the death of its emir Badr ibn Hasanawayh. He studied jurisprudence under Abu al-Husayn Ibn al-Qattan and wrote works on the school. He was proverbial for his memorization of Shafi'i jurisprudence, so that some preferred him over the shaykh of the Shafi'is, Abu Hamid al-Isfarayini, and he was known for generosity and great wealth.

en.title: The death of the Almoravid emir Tashfin ibn Ali near Oran
en.body: On the eve of the 27th of Ramadan 539 AH, the emir Tashfin ibn Ali ibn Yusuf ibn Tashfin, ruler of the Almoravid state, met his death near Oran. He had gone out at night from his besieged position to raid the camp of the Almohads under Abd al-Mu'min ibn Ali, and on a dark, rainy night he fell from a high cliff overlooking the sea. He had spent the short years of his rule in continuous wars with the Almohads, and with his death the collapse of the Almoravid state, which had ruled the Maghrib and al-Andalus for about seventy years, accelerated, until Marrakesh fell to the Almohads about two years later.

en.title: Death of al-Hafiz Nur al-Din al-Haythami, author of 'Majma al-Zawa'id'
en.body: On the eve of Tuesday the 29th of Ramadan 807 AH, the hadith master Nur al-Din Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Abi Bakr al-Haythami passed away in Cairo, the companion of al-Hafiz al-Iraqi, his son-in-law and constant companion in hearing hadith and travelling. He spent his life gathering the additional hadiths (zawa'id) of hadith books beyond the Six Books, compiling 'Majma al-Zawa'id wa Manba al-Fawa'id', in which he gathered the additional hadiths of the Musnad of Ahmad, al-Bazzar, Abu Ya'la and the Mu'jams of al-Tabarani along with grading their chains, and 'Mawarid al-Zam'an ila Zawa'id Ibn Hibban'. Ibn Hajar described him as having a sound nature and being constant in night prayer.

en.title: Death of the Caliph al-Nasir li-Din Allah after the longest Abbasid caliphate
en.body: On the last day of Ramadan 622 AH, the Abbasid Caliph al-Nasir li-Din Allah Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn al-Mustadi passed away in Baghdad after a caliphate of about forty-seven years, the longest reign of any Abbasid caliph. In his reign he worked to restore the prestige of the caliphate and its political influence in Iraq, and he was a contemporary of Salah al-Din al-Ayyubi and the recovery of Jerusalem. He was struck by paralysis in his final days, and after him his son al-Zahir bi-Amr Allah received the pledge of allegiance.

en.title: Death of Imam Muwaffaq al-Din Ibn Qudama al-Maqdisi
en.body: On the day of Eid al-Fitr 620 AH, Imam Muwaffaq al-Din Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Qudama al-Maqdisi, one of the leading figures of Hanbali jurisprudence, passed away in Damascus at nearly eighty years of age. He grew up in a family from Jerusalem that had emigrated to Damascus, and travelled to Baghdad seeking knowledge, then returned to teach, issue fatwas and write. Among his most famous works are 'al-Mughni' in comparative jurisprudence, 'Rawdat al-Nazir' in the principles of jurisprudence, and 'al-Umda', 'al-Muqni' and 'al-Kafi'. A huge crowd attended his funeral, and he was buried on the slope of Mount Qasiyun. His books remain a reference in jurisprudence to this day.

en.title: Death of the reciter and exegete Abu Bakr al-Naqqash
en.body: On Tuesday the 2nd of Shawwal 351 AH, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Naqqash, the shaykh of the Quran reciters in his era, passed away in Baghdad aged over eighty. He travelled in pursuit of the readings and hadith to the Levant, Egypt, al-Jazira and Khurasan, and great numbers read the Quran with him. He compiled a large exegesis called 'Shifa al-Sudur', and works on the sciences of the Quran. Some hadith scholars, such as al-Daraqutni, criticized his precision in narration, but his standing in the Quranic readings remained renowned. It is narrated that he kept repeating a verse of the Quran as he was dying until his soul departed, and he was buried in his house in Baghdad.

en.title: Death of the historian Taqi al-Din al-Fasi, historian of Makkah
en.body: At the beginning of Shawwal 832 AH, the historian and hadith scholar Taqi al-Din Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Fasi, the Maliki judge of Makkah, passed away there. He was born and raised in Makkah, travelled in pursuit of hadith, and wrote the most extensive histories of the Sacred City, among them 'al-Iqd al-Thamin fi Tarikh al-Balad al-Amin' and 'Shifa al-Gharam bi-Akhbar al-Balad al-Haram', which became the reference for everyone who wrote about Makkah and its notable figures. His student Ibn Fahd al-Makki dated his death to the eve of the 3rd of Shawwal, while al-Suyuti mentioned it was on the 2nd.

en.title: Death of the Kufan hadith scholar Ya'la ibn Ubayd al-Tanafisi
en.body: On Sunday the 5th of Shawwal 209 AH, the trustworthy hadith scholar Abu Yusuf Ya'la ibn Ubayd al-Tanafisi passed away in Kufa aged over ninety, during the caliphate of al-Ma'mun. He narrated from al-A'mash, Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari and Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, and the authors of the Six Books narrated from him. He was renowned for scrupulousness and good character, so that some of his contemporaries said they had never seen anyone who sought the Face of Allah with his knowledge as he did. He and his brothers were from a household known in Kufa for knowledge and blessing.

en.title: Death of the imam of Arabic Taj al-Din al-Kindi
en.body: On the 6th of Shawwal 613 AH, Taj al-Din Abu al-Yumn Zayd ibn al-Hasan al-Kindi passed away in Damascus at the age of ninety-three. He was an imam in grammar, language and the Quranic readings; his chains of transmission were so elevated that people travelled to him, and al-Malik al-Mu'azzam Isa al-Ayyubi studied with him, coming down from the citadel to learn. Scholars and men of letters praised him and poets eulogized him; the funeral prayer was held for him in the Umayyad Mosque and he was buried in al-Salihiyya. Among his good deeds was that he endowed his precious library, more than seven hundred volumes, to scholars and students of knowledge.

en.title: The Expedition of Hamra al-Asad
en.body: On the day after the Battle of Uhud, Sunday in Shawwal 3 AH, the Prophet ﷺ ordered his muezzin to call on the people to go out in pursuit of the Quraysh army, and that none should go out with him except those who had been present at Uhud. The Muslims set out despite their wounds until they reached Hamra al-Asad, a few miles from Madinah, and stayed there for days lighting fires, so Abu Sufyan chose to return to Makkah. Ibn Sa'd dated it to the 8th of Shawwal in line with his dating of Uhud to the 7th, while Ibn Ishaq placed it on the 16th because he dated Uhud to the middle of Shawwal.

en.title: Death of the Tabi'i Imam Muhammad ibn Sirin
en.body: On the 9th of Shawwal 110 AH, Imam Muhammad ibn Sirin al-Ansari, one of the great scholars of the Successors (Tabi'in), passed away in Basra, about a hundred days after the death of his companion al-Hasan al-Basri. He was a scrupulous jurist, trustworthy in narrating hadith, and was renowned for his extreme care in earning and dealings, as well as for his skill in interpreting dreams, so that his name became associated with that art. His contemporaries praised him for knowledge, scrupulousness and magnanimity, and he was counted among the eminent figures of Basra in its golden age.

en.title: Death of the just Sultan Nur al-Din Mahmud Zangi
en.body: On the 11th of Shawwal 569 AH, Sultan Nur al-Din Mahmud ibn Zangi passed away in Damascus at the age of fifty-eight, having ruled for nearly twenty-eight years. He united Aleppo, Damascus, Mosul and Egypt under one banner, fought the Crusaders, and was known for justice and asceticism. He founded the House of Justice (Dar al-Adl), madrasas and the Nuri Bimaristan (hospital) in Damascus, and ordered the making of the minbar that Salah al-Din later carried to al-Masjid al-Aqsa. His policies had a great impact in paving the way for the liberation of Jerusalem.

en.title: Martyrdom of al-Hafiz Makki al-Rumayli, historian of Jerusalem
en.body: On the 12th of Shawwal 492 AH, the hadith master Abu al-Qasim Makki ibn Abd al-Salam al-Rumayli al-Maqdisi was killed, after the Crusaders had taken him captive when they seized Jerusalem in Sha'ban of that year. He was a travelling hadith scholar who had journeyed through Egypt, the Levant and Iraq, and a Shafi'i jurist to whom questions for fatwas came from Egypt, the coast and Damascus, and he had begun writing a history of Jerusalem. Some historians mentioned that he was killed on the day the Franks entered the city in Sha'ban, and his life remained a testimony to the ordeal of scholars in that period.

en.title: Birth of Imam Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari
en.body: On the 13th of Shawwal 194 AH, on Friday after the prayer, Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari was born in Bukhara, who became the Commander of the Faithful in Hadith. He grew up an orphan in the care of his mother, began seeking hadith at a young age, then travelled to the Hijaz, Iraq, the Levant and Egypt. He compiled 'al-Jami al-Sahih', which the Ummah received with acceptance and regarded as the most authentic book after the Book of Allah, along with 'al-Tarikh al-Kabir' and 'al-Adab al-Mufrad'. The hadith scholars recorded the date of his birth with a precision that shows their care for the biographies of their imams.

en.title: The Expedition against Banu Qaynuqa
en.body: In mid-Shawwal of the second year after the Hijrah, about a month after the Battle of Badr, the Prophet ﷺ marched against the Jews of Banu Qaynuqa in Madinah after they had broken the covenant between him and them. They fortified themselves in their strongholds, and the Muslims besieged them for fifteen nights until they surrendered on terms of exile, leaving Madinah for Adhri'at in the Levant. This was the first confrontation between the Muslims and the Jews of Madinah, and it contributed to consolidating the security of the nascent state. Al-Waqidi mentioned that it was on Saturday, the middle of Shawwal.

en.title: Death of Imam Abu Dawud al-Sijistani, author of the Sunan
en.body: In mid-Shawwal 275 AH, Imam Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn al-Ash'ath al-Sijistani passed away in Basra, author of the 'Sunan', one of the six canonical books of hadith. He travelled in pursuit of hadith to Khurasan, Iraq, the Levant, Egypt and the Hijaz, and studied under Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal and others. In his Sunan he gathered the hadiths of legal rulings, selecting them from hundreds of thousands, so his book became a reference for jurists. He was buried in Basra beside the grave of Sufyan al-Thawri, at the age of seventy-three.

en.title: Death of the travelling hadith master Abu Sa'd al-Malini
en.body: On Tuesday the 17th of Shawwal 412 AH, the ascetic hadith master Abu Sa'd Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Malini al-Harawi passed away in Egypt, one of the travelling hadith scholars from among the Sufis. He journeyed through Khurasan, Iraq, the Hijaz, the Levant and Egypt, heard from Ibn Adi, Abu al-Shaykh al-Asbahani and others, and wrote and copied a great deal, so that he became known for the accuracy of his transcription; he was trustworthy and meticulous. Among his works is 'al-Arba'in fi Shuyukh al-Sufiyya'. He is regarded as an example of the scholars who combined travelling in pursuit of hadith with asceticism.

en.title: Birth of Sultan Nur al-Din Mahmud Zangi in Aleppo
en.body: At sunrise on Sunday the 17th of Shawwal 511 AH, Nur al-Din Mahmud ibn Imad al-Din Zangi was born in Aleppo, who became one of the greatest rulers of his era. He grew up under the care of his father, ruler of Aleppo and Mosul, then inherited the rule of Aleppo after his father was killed in 541 AH. He united the Levant and annexed Egypt to it, and fought the Crusaders. He was known for justice, asceticism and the founding of madrasas, houses of hadith and hospitals, and through his policies he paved the way for the liberation of Jerusalem at the hands of Salah al-Din. He also died in Shawwal, in 569 AH.

en.title: Death of the jurist Abu Sa'd al-Mutawalli, author of 'Tatimmat al-Ibana'
en.body: On the eve of Friday the 18th of Shawwal 478 AH, the Shafi'i jurist Abu Sa'd Abd al-Rahman ibn Ma'mun al-Mutawalli passed away in Baghdad at about fifty-two years of age. He studied jurisprudence in Merv, Merv al-Rudh and Bukhara, then taught at the Nizamiyya madrasa in Baghdad after the death of Shaykh Abu Ishaq al-Shirazi. Among his most famous works is 'Tatimmat al-Ibana', with which he completed the book of his teacher al-Furani, gathering in it rare issues and juristic views, so that it became one of the references of the Shafi'i school. He also wrote a summary on inheritance law and a work on the foundations of religion. He was buried in the Bab Abraz cemetery.

en.title: Death of Shaykh Abu Hamid al-Isfarayini, imam of the Shafi'is in Baghdad
en.body: On the eve of Saturday with eleven nights remaining in Shawwal 406 AH, Shaykh Abu Hamid Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Isfarayini, the shaykh of the Shafi'is in Iraq in his time, passed away in Baghdad. He came to Baghdad as a young man and studied jurisprudence there until leadership of the school passed to him; hundreds of jurists attended his circle, and he wrote a great commentary (ta'liqa) on 'Mukhtasar al-Muzani' that became the basis of the Iraqi method within the school. The funeral prayer was held for him in the open country with a great gathering, and he was buried in his house and later moved. Scholars praised him for knowledge and religion.

en.title: Death of al-Rabi ibn Sulayman al-Muradi, narrator of al-Shafi'i's books
en.body: On the 20th of Shawwal 270 AH, al-Rabi ibn Sulayman al-Muradi passed away in Egypt, the student of Imam al-Shafi'i and narrator of his books, among them 'al-Umm' and 'al-Risala' in their Egyptian recension. He was a muezzin at the Mosque of Amr ibn al-As in Fustat, and accompanied al-Shafi'i for years until he became the most reliable of people in narrating his books, so that students of knowledge travelled to him from distant lands to hear them from him. It is mentioned that he was the first to dictate hadith in the Mosque of Ibn Tulun. Thanks to his narration, the books of al-Shafi'i upon which his school was built have reached us.

en.title: Death of al-Fayruzabadi, author of 'al-Qamus al-Muhit'
en.body: On the eve of the 20th of Shawwal 817 AH, Majd al-Din Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Fayruzabadi passed away in the city of Zabid in Yemen, at nearly ninety years of age. He was born in Kazerun in Persia, and travelled through Iraq, the Levant, Egypt, the Hijaz and India as a student and teacher, then became chief judge of Yemen. He is famous for his dictionary 'al-Qamus al-Muhit', which became one of the most famous and widely used Arabic dictionaries, and on which al-Zabidi wrote the commentary 'Taj al-Arus'. He is counted among the imams of language who served Arabic through compilation and editing.

en.title: Death of Harmala ibn Yahya al-Tujibi, companion of Imam al-Shafi'i
en.body: On the eve of Thursday with nine days remaining in Shawwal 243 AH, the jurist and hadith scholar Harmala ibn Yahya al-Tujibi passed away in Egypt, one of the closest students of Imam al-Shafi'i in Egypt and narrator of many of his statements and books in his new school. He also heard extensively from Abdullah ibn Wahb, so that it was said he had all of Ibn Wahb's hadith, and Imam Muslim narrated from him in his Sahih, as did Ibn Majah, Abu Zur'a and Abu Hatim. He is regarded as one of the pillars of transmitting Shafi'i jurisprudence in its first generation in Egypt.

en.title: Death of Emir Sayf al-Din al-Mashtub, commander of the garrison of Acre
en.body: On the 23rd of Shawwal 588 AH, Emir Sayf al-Din Ali ibn Ahmad al-Mashtub al-Hakkari passed away in Jerusalem, one of the senior emirs of Sultan Salah al-Din al-Ayyubi and leader of the Kurds in his army. He accompanied Asad al-Din Shirkuh in his campaigns on Egypt, then was Salah al-Din's deputy over Acre during its long siege; when it fell to the Crusaders he was captured and ransomed himself for a large sum, and Salah al-Din honoured him and appointed him over Nablus. The sources differ on the day of his death, between the 22nd and the 26th of Shawwal.

en.title: Death of the jurist Asbagh ibn al-Faraj, scholar of the Malikis in Egypt
en.body: On Sunday with four days remaining in Shawwal 225 AH, the jurist Asbagh ibn al-Faraj, an Umayyad by clientage, passed away in Egypt, one of the great imams of the Maliki school in Egypt. He studied jurisprudence under Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, Abdullah ibn Wahb and Ashhab, and Yahya ibn Ma'in said of him that he was among the most knowledgeable of Allah's creation of Malik's opinion, knowing it issue by issue. Al-Bukhari narrated from him in his Sahih; he was a reference for fatwas in his time, many later scholars relied on his views in the Maliki books, and he was a scribe for Ibn Wahb.

en.title: Death of the erudite Ibn al-Hajib, author of 'al-Kafiya' and 'al-Shafiya'
en.body: In the forenoon of Thursday the 26th of Shawwal 646 AH, the erudite scholar Jamal al-Din Abu Amr Uthman ibn Umar, known as Ibn al-Hajib, the Maliki jurist, grammarian, legal theorist and Quran reciter, passed away in Alexandria. He was born in Esna in Upper Egypt and studied in Cairo and Damascus. Among his most famous works are 'al-Kafiya' in grammar, 'al-Shafiya' in morphology, 'Mukhtasar al-Muntaha' in the principles of jurisprudence, and 'Jami al-Ummahat' in Maliki jurisprudence; students used them for centuries and many commentaries were written on them in the East and the West.

en.title: The killing of the Abbasid Caliph al-Muqtadir Billah
en.body: In late Shawwal 320 AH, the Abbasid Caliph al-Muqtadir Billah Ja'far ibn al-Mu'tadid was killed outside Baghdad at Bab al-Shammasiyya, in fighting with the troops of the commander Mu'nis al-Khadim, who had marched from Mosul demanding the soldiers' pay. Al-Muqtadir had assumed the caliphate as a boy of thirteen, and his caliphate lasted about twenty-five years, among the longest Abbasid caliphates, but it witnessed the weakening of central authority and the domination of commanders and viziers. After him his brother Muhammad received the pledge of allegiance and was titled al-Qahir Billah.

en.title: Death of the imam of exegetes Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari
en.body: On the evening of Sunday, two days before the end of Shawwal 310 AH, Imam Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari passed away in Baghdad aged over eighty. He was born in Amol in Tabaristan, travelled the lands in pursuit of knowledge, then settled in Baghdad writing and teaching. He left two great encyclopedic works: 'Jami al-Bayan an Ta'wil Ay al-Quran', which became the foundation of exegesis based on transmitted reports, and 'Tarikh al-Rusul wa al-Muluk', which became the main source for historians after him. He was buried in his house in Baghdad, and was known for asceticism, contentment and breadth of knowledge.

en.title: Death of the Caliph al-Mustadi and allegiance to al-Nasir li-Din Allah
en.body: On the last day of Shawwal 575 AH, the Abbasid Caliph al-Mustadi bi-Amr Allah passed away in Baghdad, and his son Abu al-Abbas Ahmad, titled al-Nasir li-Din Allah, received the pledge of allegiance. Al-Mustadi's reign saw the return of the Friday sermon in the name of the Abbasid caliphate in Egypt at the hands of Salah al-Din after the end of the Fatimid state, and Ibn al-Jawzi described him as just and generous. Al-Nasir's caliphate lasted forty-seven years, making him the longest-reigning Abbasid caliph. Some historians mentioned that the general pledge of allegiance to al-Nasir was at the beginning of Dhu al-Qa'dah.

en.title: Death of Imam Abu Ja'far al-Tahawi
en.body: At the beginning of Dhu al-Qa'dah 321 AH, Imam Abu Ja'far Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tahawi passed away in Egypt aged over eighty. He was the son of Imam al-Muzani's sister; he first studied the school of al-Shafi'i, then moved to the school of Abu Hanifa until leadership of the Hanafis in Egypt passed to him. He combined jurisprudence and hadith, and wrote 'Sharh Ma'ani al-Athar', 'Sharh Mushkil al-Athar', and books on legal documents, the disagreements of scholars and the rulings of the Quran. 'Al-Aqida al-Tahawiyya', the concise creed that Ahl al-Sunnah received with acceptance, is attributed to him.

en.title: Death of the Imam of Imams Ibn Khuzayma, author of 'al-Sahih'
en.body: At the beginning of Dhu al-Qa'dah 311 AH, Imam Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Khuzayma al-Sulami, titled the Imam of Imams, passed away in Nishapur at the age of eighty-nine. He travelled to Iraq, the Levant, al-Jazira and Egypt, studied jurisprudence under al-Muzani and others, and al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated from him outside their Sahihs. He compiled 'al-Sahih', known as Sahih Ibn Khuzayma, and 'Kitab al-Tawhid', and was proverbial for his memorization of chains and texts and for his asceticism and generosity. Al-Dhahabi dated his death to the 2nd of Dhu al-Qa'dah, citing the History of Nishapur, while Ibn al-Jawzi mentioned it was on the 8th.

en.title: Death of Imam al-Hafiz Shams al-Din al-Dhahabi, historian of Islam
en.body: On the eve of Monday the 3rd of Dhu al-Qa'dah 748 AH, the hadith master Shams al-Din Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Uthman al-Dhahabi passed away in Damascus, having lost his sight at the end of his life. He was a hadith scholar, historian and critic of narrators, and left works that became the main reference for those after him, the most famous being 'Tarikh al-Islam', 'Siyar A'lam al-Nubala', 'Mizan al-I'tidal' and 'Tadhkirat al-Huffaz'. The funeral prayer was held for him in the Umayyad Mosque and he was buried in the Bab al-Saghir cemetery. His student Ibn Kathir said that with him the line of the shaykhs and masters of hadith came to a close.

en.title: Death of al-Hafiz Abd al-Azim al-Mundhiri, author of 'al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib'
en.body: On the 4th of Dhu al-Qa'dah 656 AH, the hadith master Zaki al-Din Abd al-Azim ibn Abd al-Qawi al-Mundhiri passed away in Cairo, shaykh of Dar al-Hadith al-Kamiliyya in Egypt. He was an imam in hadith, its hidden defects and knowledge of its narrators, a Shafi'i jurist with mastery of the language, and a number of hadith masters graduated under him, among them Sharaf al-Din al-Dimyati. Among his most famous works is 'al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib', still in circulation in mosques and homes, along with his abridgements of Sahih Muslim and Sunan Abi Dawud. He was buried in al-Qarafa.

en.title: Death of Sultan al-Mansur Qalawun, builder of the Mansuri Bimaristan
en.body: On the 6th of Dhu al-Qa'dah 689 AH, the Mamluk Sultan al-Mansur Qalawun al-Salihi passed away in his camp outside Cairo while preparing to march on Acre, the last major Crusader stronghold on the Levantine coast. He ruled for about twelve years, defeated the Mongols at Homs, and conquered Tripoli in the Levant in 688 AH. He left behind in Bayn al-Qasrayn in Cairo a great complex comprising a madrasa, a house of hadith and a hospital (bimaristan) that continued treating the sick for centuries. He was succeeded by his son al-Ashraf Khalil, who completed the conquest of Acre months later.

en.title: Death of Imam al-Daraqutni, Commander of the Faithful in Hadith
en.body: In Dhu al-Qa'dah 385 AH, Imam Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Umar al-Daraqutni passed away in Baghdad at the age of seventy-nine and was buried in the cemetery of Ma'ruf al-Karkhi. He combined knowledge of hadith and its hidden defects with the Quranic readings, grammar, jurisprudence and literature, so that al-Hakim said he had never seen anyone like him. Among his most famous books are 'al-Sunan', 'al-Ilal' and 'al-Ilzamat wa al-Tatabbu' on the two Sahihs. Al-Dhahabi and al-Suyuti dated his death to the 8th of Dhu al-Qa'dah, while Ibn Kathir mentioned it was on Tuesday the 7th.

en.title: Death of Shaykh al-Islam Siraj al-Din al-Bulqini
en.body: On Friday the 10th of Dhu al-Qa'dah 805 AH, Shaykh al-Islam Siraj al-Din Umar ibn Raslan al-Bulqini passed away in Cairo, the jurist of the Shafi'is in his era and one of the great mujtahids within their school. He held the office of mufti of Dar al-Adl and was judge of Damascus for a time, taught at the major madrasas of Cairo such as al-Khashshabiyya and al-Zahiriyya, and taught exegesis at the Mosque of Ibn Tulun. Among his works are 'Mahasin al-Istilah' on the sciences of hadith and commentaries on al-Bukhari and al-Tirmidhi. He had scholarly sons, among them Jalal al-Din al-Bulqini, who succeeded him in his standing.

en.title: Opening of the Nizamiyya madrasa in Baghdad
en.body: On Saturday the 10th of Dhu al-Qa'dah 459 AH, the Nizamiyya madrasa founded by the Seljuk vizier Nizam al-Mulk opened in Baghdad, about two years after construction began. Shaykh Abu Ishaq al-Shirazi was to teach there, but when he delayed coming, Abu Nasr Ibn al-Sabbagh, author of 'al-Shamil', was appointed in his place; Abu Ishaq then returned to it after about twenty days. The Nizamiyya became a model for a network of madrasas that spread through the cities of the East, and eminent figures such as Abu Hamid al-Ghazali later taught there.

sources: ابن الجوزي، المنتظم في تاريخ الملوك والأمم، ج13 ص77 (وفيات 295هـ) — https://shamela.ws/book/12406/4310

en.title: Death of the Abbasid Caliph al-Muktafi Billah
en.body: On the eve of Sunday the 12th of Dhu al-Qa'dah 295 AH, the Abbasid Caliph al-Muktafi Billah Ali ibn al-Mu'tadid passed away in Baghdad at the age of thirty-two, after a caliphate of about six years. He inherited a stable state from his father; in his reign the caliphate recovered Egypt and the Levant from the Tulunid state in 292 AH, and his armies fought the Qarmatians in the Levant. When his illness worsened he designated his brother Ja'far as successor, who received the pledge of allegiance after him with the title al-Muqtadir Billah, a boy of thirteen, the youngest to assume the caliphate up to that time.

en.title: Death of the hadith scholar and jurist Abu al-Tahir ibn al-Sarh al-Misri
en.body: On Monday the 14th of Dhu al-Qa'dah, the jurist and hadith scholar Abu al-Tahir Ahmad ibn Amr ibn al-Sarh, an Umayyad by clientage, passed away in Egypt, one of the teachers of Imam Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah. He narrated extensively from Abdullah ibn Wahb, and from Imam al-Shafi'i, Sufyan ibn Uyayna and al-Walid ibn Muslim, and the historian of Egypt Ibn Yunus described him as a jurist among the righteous and reliable. Al-Suyuti dated his death to 250 AH, while Ibn Hajar mentioned 255 AH in Tahdhib al-Tahdhib, though they agree on the day and month.

en.title: Death of Sultan al-Muzaffar Qutuz, hero of Ayn Jalut
en.body: On the 16th of Dhu al-Qa'dah 658 AH, the Mamluk Sultan al-Muzaffar Sayf al-Din Qutuz was killed on his way back to Egypt, between al-Ghazali and al-Salihiyya, by a group of emirs, less than two months after his great victory over the Mongols at Ayn Jalut. He had assumed the sultanate about a year earlier to unite the ranks against the Mongol threat, and Ibn Kathir described him as righteous, frequent in congregational prayer and beloved by the people. Al-Zahir Baybars assumed the sultanate after him.

en.title: Death of Sitt al-Sham bint Ayyub, founder of the two Shamiyya madrasas
en.body: On Friday the 16th of Dhu al-Qa'dah 616 AH, Sitt al-Sham bint Najm al-Din Ayyub, sister of Sultan Salah al-Din al-Ayyubi, passed away in Damascus. She was among the most charitable and beneficent women of her era; every year she had drinks and medicines prepared in her house worth thousands of dinars and distributed them to the needy. She endowed two madrasas known as al-Shamiyya al-Juwwaniyya inside Damascus and al-Shamiyya al-Barraniyya outside it, which became among the most important Shafi'i madrasas in the city. She died in her house, which she had made into a madrasa, and was then moved to her mausoleum at al-Shamiyya al-Barraniyya.
