en.title: Al-Zahir Baybars assumes the sultanate of Egypt and the Levant
en.body: On the 17th of Dhu al-Qa'dah 658 AH, Emir Rukn al-Din Baybars al-Bunduqdari assumed the Mamluk sultanate in Egypt and the Levant and was titled al-Malik al-Zahir. He was one of the Mamluks of al-Malik al-Salih Ayyub, and fought at the Battle of al-Mansura against the Seventh Crusade, then at the Battle of Ayn Jalut. His rule lasted about seventeen years, during which he revived the Abbasid caliphate in Cairo, conquered many Crusader fortresses such as Caesarea, Jaffa, Antioch and Krak des Chevaliers (Hisn al-Akrad), repelled the Mongols, and established the express postal system between Cairo and Damascus.

en.title: Death of al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar, judge of Makkah and genealogist of Quraysh
en.body: On the eve of Sunday with nine days remaining in Dhu al-Qa'dah 256 AH, al-Qadi Abu Abdullah al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar, a descendant of the Companion al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam (may Allah be pleased with him), passed away in Makkah at the age of eighty-four. He served as judge of Makkah, and came to Baghdad where he narrated hadith; he was among the most knowledgeable of people in the genealogies of the Arabs and the reports of earlier generations. Among his most famous works is 'Jamharat Nasab Quraysh wa Akhbariha', which became a foundation for those after him in genealogy, and 'al-Akhbar al-Muwaffaqiyyat'. Al-Daraqutni and al-Khatib al-Baghdadi declared him trustworthy, and Ibn Majah narrated from him.

en.title: Death of al-Qadi Abu Bakr al-Baqillani
en.body: On Saturday with seven days remaining in Dhu al-Qa'dah 403 AH, al-Qadi Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Tayyib al-Baqillani passed away in Baghdad, one of the most prominent theologians of Ahl al-Sunnah and imams of the Ash'ari school, and a Maliki jurist. He was known for the strength of his arguments and quick wit in debate, and Adud al-Dawla sent him as an envoy to the Byzantine king in Constantinople, where he debated their scholars. Among his works are 'I'jaz al-Quran', 'al-Tamhid' and 'al-Intisar li-l-Quran'. He was buried in his house and later moved to the Bab Harb cemetery in Baghdad.

en.title: Death of al-Hafiz al-Tabarani, author of the three Mu'jams
en.body: In late Dhu al-Qa'dah 360 AH, the hadith master Abu al-Qasim Sulayman ibn Ahmad al-Tabarani passed away in Isfahan, having completed a hundred years. He travelled in pursuit of hadith for more than thirty years among the Levant, the Hijaz, Yemen, Egypt, Iraq and Persia, and heard from about a thousand shaykhs. Among his most famous works are 'al-Mu'jam al-Kabir', 'al-Mu'jam al-Awsat' and 'al-Mu'jam al-Saghir', among the most extensive collections of hadith. Al-Dhahabi reported from Abu Nu'aym, and Ibn Kathir from Ibn Khallikan, that he died on Saturday with two nights remaining in the month, while al-Suyuti mentioned that he died with three remaining.

en.title: Death of al-Malik al-Mu'azzam Isa al-Ayyubi, ruler of Damascus
en.body: On Friday, the last day of Dhu al-Qa'dah 624 AH, or it is said the beginning of Dhu al-Hijjah, al-Malik al-Mu'azzam Sharaf al-Din Isa ibn al-Malik al-Adil al-Ayyubi, nephew of Salah al-Din, passed away in Damascus. His realm extended from Homs to al-Arish and included Jerusalem and al-Karak, and he fought valiantly against the Crusade on Damietta. He was a scholar who loved scholars; he studied Hanafi jurisprudence, studied grammar with Taj al-Din al-Kindi, set a prize for whoever memorized al-Zamakhshari's 'al-Mufassal', and ordered the arrangement of Imam Ahmad's 'Musnad'. He was buried in the al-Mu'azzamiyya madrasa on the slope of Qasiyun.

en.title: Death of al-Hafiz Ibn Manda, the travelling hadith scholar of Isfahan
en.body: On the last day of Dhu al-Qa'dah 395 AH, the hadith master Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Manda passed away in Isfahan, one of the most widely travelled hadith scholars in Islamic history. He journeyed the world for over thirty years, heard from about one thousand seven hundred shaykhs, and returned to his city with loads of books. Among his works are 'Ma'rifat al-Sahaba', 'Kitab al-Iman' and 'al-Tawhid'. His student Abu Nu'aym al-Asbahani dated his death to the last day of Dhu al-Qa'dah.

en.title: Death of Imam al-Hawfi, author of al-Burhan fi Ulum al-Quran
en.body: In Egypt, at the beginning of Dhu al-Hijjah 430 AH, the grammarian Imam Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'id al-Hawfi passed away, one of the great scholars of Arabic and exegesis in Egypt, and a student of Abu Bakr al-Udfuwi, who learned from Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas. Among his most famous works is al-Burhan fi Ulum al-Quran, a large exegesis concerned with the grammatical analysis and meanings of the verses, and a book on the grammatical analysis of the Quran from which the people of Egypt benefited. Ibn Khallikan, al-Safadi and al-Suyuti stated that his death was at the beginning of Dhu al-Hijjah.

sources: البخاري، الصحيح، كتاب الحج (من رواية ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما): يذكر قدوم النبي ﷺ مكة لأربع ليال خلون من ذي الحجة — https://app.turath.io/book/735?page=4738

en.title: The Prophet ﷺ arrives in Makkah for the Farewell Pilgrimage
en.body: In Dhu al-Hijjah 10 AH, the Prophet ﷺ arrived in Makkah for the Farewell Pilgrimage, having left Madinah in late Dhu al-Qa'dah accompanied by great numbers of Muslims. Authentic narrations mention that he arrived on the 4th of Dhu al-Hijjah, on Sunday morning; he performed tawaf around the House and sa'i between al-Safa and al-Marwa, and remained in ihram because he had brought the sacrificial animals, then camped in upper Makkah until he went out to Mina on the Day of Tarwiyah. This was the only Hajj he ﷺ performed after the Hijrah.

en.title: Death of the grammarian Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas, author of I'rab al-Quran
en.body: In Egypt, the grammarian Imam Abu Ja'far Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isma'il, known as al-Nahhas, passed away, one of the leading figures of Arabic in the fourth century AH. He had travelled to Baghdad and learned from al-Akhfash al-Saghir, al-Zajjaj and Niftawayh, then returned to Egypt where great numbers benefited from him. Among his most famous works are I'rab al-Quran, Ma'ani al-Quran, and al-Nasikh wa al-Mansukh. Ibn Khallikan and al-Tanukhi mentioned that he died on Saturday the 5th of Dhu al-Hijjah 338 AH, drowning in the Nile at the Nilometer, while some placed it in 337 AH.

en.title: The Expedition of al-Sawiq
en.body: After the Battle of Badr, Abu Sufyan ibn Harb vowed to raid Madinah. He set out with about two hundred riders and raided the area of al-Urayd, burning palm trees and killing two men. When the Prophet ﷺ learned of it, he went out in pursuit of him on Sunday the 5th of Dhu al-Hijjah 2 AH. Abu Sufyan and his companions fled and began throwing away the sacks of sawiq (barley meal) that were their provisions to lighten their mounts; the Muslims took them as spoils, and the expedition was named after it. The Prophet ﷺ returned to Madinah without fighting, and some historians mentioned that it was in Safar.

en.title: Death of the Caliph Abu Ja'far al-Mansur in ihram near Makkah
en.body: In Dhu al-Hijjah 158 AH, the Abbasid Caliph Abu Ja'far Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Mansur passed away at Bi'r Maymun near Makkah. He had set out for Hajj and his illness worsened on the way, so he died in the state of ihram and was buried there. Al-Mansur was the founder of the city of Baghdad and built the pillars of the Abbasid state during twenty-two years of rule. Al-Tabari mentioned that his death was on the eve of Saturday the 6th of Dhu al-Hijjah, and al-Dhahabi agreed, while al-Ya'qubi placed it on the 3rd.

en.title: Death of the astronomer Nasir al-Din al-Tusi, builder of the Maragha Observatory
en.body: In Baghdad in 672 AH, the astronomer and mathematician Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Tusi, known as Nasir al-Din al-Tusi, passed away, one of the most prominent scholars of astronomy and mathematics in his era. He founded the great Maragha Observatory, gathering scholars and a huge library there, and wrote Tahrir Usul Uqlidis (a recension of Euclid's Elements), al-Tadhkira fi Ilm al-Hay'a, and al-Zij al-Ilkhani, and his works influenced astronomy after him. Ibn Kathir and Hajji Khalifa mentioned that his death was on the 12th of Dhu al-Hijjah, and it is also said the 18th, when he had reached seventy-five years of age.

en.title: The Second Pledge of al-Aqabah
en.body: During the Hajj season, months before the Hijrah, the Prophet ﷺ met at night at al-Aqabah in Mina with a delegation of the Ansar from al-Aws and al-Khazraj numbering seventy-three men and two women, in the presence of his uncle al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib. They pledged to support and protect him if he emigrated to them, and he chose twelve leaders (naqibs) from among them. Ka'b ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) and Ibn Ishaq mentioned that the appointment was in the middle of the Days of Tashriq, that is, around the 12th of Dhu al-Hijjah. This pledge was the direct preparation for the emigration of the Muslims to Madinah.

sources: الطبري، تاريخ الرسل والملوك، الجزء السابع، سنة 136: (وفيها توفي أبو العباس أمير المؤمنين بالأنبار يوم الأحد، لثلاث عشرة خلت من ذي الحجة) — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/تاريخ_الطبري/الجزء_السابع

en.title: Death of Abu al-Abbas al-Saffah, first of the Abbasid caliphs
en.body: In Dhu al-Hijjah 136 AH, Abu al-Abbas Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Saffah, the first caliph of the Abbasid state, passed away in the city of al-Anbar, which he had taken as the seat of his rule. His illness was smallpox, and his caliphate did not exceed four years and some months. Before his death he designated as caliph his brother Abu Ja'far al-Mansur, who established the pillars of the state after him. The best-known view in al-Tabari and Ibn Abd Rabbih is that he died on the 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah, while Hisham al-Kalbi mentioned the 12th, and Ibn Kathir reported a view of the 11th.

sources: ابن إياس، جواهر السلوك في أمر الخلفاء والملوك، ج1 ص324: (ودفن في يوم أحد ثالث عشر ذي الحجة سنة إحدى وأربعين وثمانمائة) — https://app.turath.io/book/30068?page=321

en.title: Death of Sultan al-Ashraf Barsbay, conqueror of Cyprus
en.body: In Cairo in 841 AH, the Mamluk Sultan al-Malik al-Ashraf Sayf al-Din Barsbay passed away after about sixteen years in power, and his son al-Aziz Yusuf assumed the sultanate after him. Among the most prominent events of his reign were the naval campaigns on Cyprus that ended with the capture of its king, securing the coasts of the Levant and Egypt from pirate raids, and the founding of the al-Ashrafiyya madrasa and the mosque in al-Khanqah. Ibn Iyas, al-Biqa'i and al-Maqrizi mentioned that his death was on Saturday the 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah, and he was buried in his mausoleum in the desert (al-Sahra).

sources: المحبي، خلاصة الأثر في أعيان القرن الحادي عشر، ترجمة ابن العماد: (وكان قد حج فمات بمكة وكانت وفاته سادس عشر ذي الحجة سنة تسع وثمانين وألف ودفن بالمعلاة) — https://tarajm.com/people/57378

en.title: Death of Ibn al-Imad al-Hanbali, author of Shadharat al-Dhahab, in Makkah
en.body: In Makkah in 1089 AH, the historian and jurist Abu al-Falah Abd al-Hayy ibn Ahmad Ibn al-Imad al-Akri al-Hanbali al-Dimashqi passed away; he had set out for Hajj and death overtook him after performing the rites, and he was buried in al-Ma'la. He grew up in al-Salihiyya in Damascus and lived in Cairo for a long time to learn from its scholars. Among his most famous works is Shadharat al-Dhahab fi Akhbar man Dhahab, a history arranged by year from the Hijrah to 1000 AH, and a commentary on the text of al-Muntaha in jurisprudence. Al-Muhibbi mentioned that his death was on the 16th of Dhu al-Hijjah.

sources: الذهبي، تذكرة الحفاظ، الطبقة الخامسة عشرة، ترجمة الحميدي: (مات في سابع عشر ذي الحجة سنة ثمان وثمانين وأربعمائة وأمهم عليه الإمام أبو بكر الشاشي) — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/تذكرة_الحفاظ/الطبقة_الخامسة_عشرة

en.title: Death of al-Hafiz al-Humaydi, author of al-Jam bayn al-Sahihayn
en.body: In Baghdad in 488 AH, the hadith master Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Futuh al-Humaydi al-Andalusi al-Mayurqi passed away, a student of Ibn Hazm and Ibn Abd al-Barr, who travelled from al-Andalus to the East in pursuit of hadith and settled in Baghdad. Among his most famous books are al-Jam bayn al-Sahihayn and Jadhwat al-Muqtabis fi Dhikr Wulat al-Andalus wa Ulama'iha. Al-Dhahabi and Ibn Khallikan, citing al-Sam'ani, mentioned that he died on the eve of Tuesday the 17th of Dhu al-Hijjah; Abu Bakr al-Shashi led the funeral prayer over him, and two years later he was moved to be buried near the grave of Bishr al-Hafi as he had requested.

sources: الذهبي، تذهيب تهذيب الكمال، ج3 ص15، ترجمة حماد بن سلمة نقلًا عن ابن حبان: (قال ابن حبان: مات لإحدى عشرة ليلة بقيت من ذي الحجة سنة سبع وستين ومائة) — https://app.turath.io/book/149213?page=881

en.title: Death of Imam Hammad ibn Salama, the hadith scholar of Basra
en.body: In Basra in 167 AH, Imam Abu Salama Hammad ibn Salama ibn Dinar passed away, one of the imams of hadith and Arabic in his era. He was among the most reliable of people in narrating from Thabit al-Bunani, and Sibawayh and Yunus learned Arabic from him. He was known for worship, asceticism and openly upholding the Sunnah, and Ibn al-Mubarak, Ibn Mahdi and great numbers narrated from him. Ibn Hibban mentioned that he died with eleven nights remaining in Dhu al-Hijjah, and al-Mada'ini mentioned that it was on a Tuesday in Dhu al-Hijjah 167 AH, which corresponds to the 19th.

sources: الذهبي، تذكرة الحفاظ، الطبقة الثامنة عشرة، ترجمة الكلاعي نقلًا عن ابن الأبار: (استشهد بكائنة أينشة على ثلاثة فراسخ من مرسية مقبلا غير مدبر في العشرين من ذي الحجة سنة أربع وثلاثين وستمائة) — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/تذكرة_الحفاظ/الطبقة_الثامنة_عشرة

en.title: Martyrdom of al-Hafiz Abu al-Rabi al-Kala'i, hadith scholar of al-Andalus
en.body: In Dhu al-Hijjah 634 AH, the hadith master Abu al-Rabi Sulayman ibn Musa al-Kala'i al-Balansi, the shaykh of hadith and eloquence in al-Andalus, was martyred at the Battle of Anisha near Valencia, fighting while advancing and not retreating, at nearly seventy years of age. He was an imam in the craft of hadith and knowledge of narrators, and an eloquent orator who spoke on behalf of the emirs at gatherings. Among his most famous works is al-Iktifa fi Maghazi Rasul Allah ﷺ wa al-Khulafa al-Thalatha. Al-Dhahabi reported from his student Ibn al-Abbar that his martyrdom was on the 20th of Dhu al-Hijjah.

sources: ابن قطلوبغا، تاج التراجم، ترجمة يوسف بن قزغلي: (توفي ليلة الثلاثاء، حادي عشرين ذي الحجة، سنة أربع وخمسين وستمائة) — https://tarajm.com/people/72040

en.title: Death of the historian Sibt Ibn al-Jawzi, author of Mir'at al-Zaman
en.body: In Damascus in 654 AH, the historian and preacher Abu al-Muzaffar Yusuf ibn Qizoghlu passed away, known as Sibt Ibn al-Jawzi because he was the grandson of Imam Abu al-Faraj Ibn al-Jawzi through his mother. He grew up in Baghdad and then settled in Damascus; he was an eloquent preacher whose assemblies drew great crowds, and a jurist who moved to the school of Abu Hanifa. Among his most famous works is Mir'at al-Zaman fi Tarikh al-A'yan, one of the most extensive works of general history. His biographers mentioned that his death was on the eve of Tuesday the 21st of Dhu al-Hijjah.

sources: ابن كثير، البداية والنهاية، الجزء الحادي عشر، سنة 282، ترجمة إسماعيل بن إسحاق: (كانت وفاته فجأة ليلة الأربعاء لثمان بقين من ذي الحجة منها، وقد جاوز الثمانين) — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/البداية_والنهاية/الجزء_الحادي_عشر/ثم_دخلت_سنة_ثنتين_وثمانين_ومائتين

en.title: Death of al-Qadi Isma'il ibn Ishaq, shaykh of the Malikis in Iraq
en.body: In Baghdad in 282 AH, al-Qadi Abu Ishaq Isma'il ibn Ishaq al-Azdi al-Basri, the shaykh of the Malikis in Iraq, died suddenly; he had served as judge and then became the foremost of the judges in the reign of al-Mu'tadid. He combined jurisprudence, hadith, the Quranic readings and Arabic, so that al-Mubarrad said he was more knowledgeable than himself in morphology, and he wrote Ahkam al-Quran and books on jurisprudence and usul. Ibn Kathir mentioned that his death was on the eve of Wednesday with eight days remaining in Dhu al-Hijjah, while Ibn al-Nadim placed it with seven remaining.

sources: ابن خلكان، وفيات الأعيان، ج5 ص59، ترجمة الإخشيد: (في الساعة الرابعة من يوم الجمعة لثمان بقين من ذي الحجة سنة أربع وثلاثين وثلثمائة بدمشق، وحمل تابوته إلى بيت المقدس) — https://app.turath.io/book/1000?page=2057

en.title: Death of al-Ikhshid, founder of the Ikhshidid state in Egypt and the Levant
en.body: In Damascus in 334 AH, Emir Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Tughj, titled al-Ikhshid, passed away, founder of the Ikhshidid state that ruled Egypt, the Levant and the Hijaz in the name of the Abbasid caliphate. He took charge of Egypt in 323 AH and restored stability after successive upheavals, and repelled the attacks of the Fatimids from the west. After his death Kafur al-Ikhshidi managed the state in the name of his sons. Ibn Khallikan, al-Maqrizi and al-Fasi mentioned that his death was on Friday with eight days remaining in Dhu al-Hijjah, and his coffin was carried to Jerusalem where he was buried.

sources: ابن كثير، البداية والنهاية، الجزء الحادي عشر، سنة 285، ترجمة إبراهيم بن إسحاق: (ثم كانت وفاته لسبع بقين من ذي الحجة وصلى عليه يوسف بن يعقوب القاضي عند باب الأنبار) — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/البداية_والنهاية/الجزء_الحادي_عشر/ثم_دخلت_سنة_خمس_وثمانين_ومائتين

en.title: Death of Imam Ibrahim al-Harbi, hadith scholar and ascetic of Baghdad
en.body: In Baghdad in 285 AH, Imam Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Harbi passed away, one of the senior companions of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal. He was an imam in hadith, jurisprudence and language, renowned for asceticism, contentment and patience in poverty along with the breadth of his knowledge. Among his most famous works is Gharib al-Hadith. Ibn Kathir and others mentioned that his death was with seven days remaining in Dhu al-Hijjah, and that his funeral was well attended by great crowds; al-Qadi Yusuf ibn Ya'qub led the funeral prayer over him at Bab al-Anbar.

sources: الطبري، تاريخ الرسل والملوك، الجزء التاسع، سنة 232: (وكانت وفاته لستٍّ بقين من ذي الحجة) — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/تاريخ_الطبري/الجزء_التاسع

en.title: Death of the Caliph al-Wathiq and allegiance to al-Mutawakkil
en.body: In Dhu al-Hijjah 232 AH, the Abbasid Caliph Harun al-Wathiq Billah ibn al-Mu'tasim passed away in Samarra after suffering from dropsy; his caliphate lasted about five and a half years. On the same day his brother Ja'far ibn al-Mu'tasim received the pledge of allegiance as caliph with the title al-Mutawakkil ala Allah, after the statesmen hesitated to appoint al-Wathiq's son because of his young age. The sources agree that this was on Wednesday with six days remaining in Dhu al-Hijjah. Al-Mutawakkil's reign later saw the ending of the Mihna (inquisition) against the scholars and the return of stability to the assemblies of hadith.

sources: ابن كثير، البداية والنهاية، الجزء السابع، ذكر بيعة علي رضي الله عنه بالخلافة: (وكانت هذه البيعة يوم الجمعة لخمس بقين من ذي الحجة) — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/البداية_والنهاية/الجزء_السابع/ذكر_بيعة_علي_رضي_الله_عنه_بالخلافة

en.title: The general pledge of allegiance to Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) as caliph
en.body: After the martyrdom of the Caliph Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him) in Madinah, the people gathered in the Prophet's Mosque and pledged allegiance to Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) as caliph, and he became the fourth of the Rightly Guided Caliphs. Ibn Kathir, Miskawayh and others mentioned that the pledge was on Friday with five days remaining in Dhu al-Hijjah 35 AH, while other narrations say it was in the days immediately following the killing of Uthman, and that Ali then addressed the people with his first sermon, praising and glorifying Allah and admonishing them. Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) inherited a turbulent state, and he strove to unite the ranks in severe circumstances.

sources: سبط ابن العجمي، كنوز الذهب في تاريخ حلب، ج2 ص219، نقلًا عن كتاب ورد من القاهرة: (يتضمن أنه توفي ليلة السبت بعد العشاء بنحو عشرين درجة ثامن عشرين ذي الحجة سنة اثنين وخمسين) — https://app.turath.io/book/11786?page=825

en.title: Death of al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani, author of Fath al-Bari
en.body: In Cairo in 852 AH, the hadith master Shihab al-Din Abu al-Fadl Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Hajar al-Asqalani passed away, the Commander of the Faithful in Hadith and Shafi'i Chief Judge of Egypt. Among his most famous works are Fath al-Bari bi-Sharh Sahih al-Bukhari, al-Isaba fi Tamyiz al-Sahaba, Tahdhib al-Tahdhib and Bulugh al-Maram. The Sultan, the notables of the state and great crowds of people attended his funeral. The view relied upon by his contemporaries is that he died on the eve of Saturday the 28th of Dhu al-Hijjah, while some books state the 18th.

sources: ابن كثير، البداية والنهاية، الجزء الثالث عشر، سنة 606، ترجمة ابن الأثير صاحب جامع الأصول والنهاية: (كانت وفاته في سلخ ذي الحجة عن ثنتين وستين سنة) — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/البداية_والنهاية/الجزء_الثالث_عشر/ثم_دخلت_سنة_ست_وستمائة

en.title: Death of Majd al-Din Ibn al-Athir, author of al-Nihaya and Jami al-Usul
en.body: In Mosul, on the last day of the year 606 AH, Imam Majd al-Din Abu al-Sa'adat al-Mubarak ibn Muhammad al-Shaybani al-Jazari, known as Ibn al-Athir, passed away, brother of the historian Izz al-Din Ibn al-Athir. He was a scholar of hadith, language and jurisprudence; he kept to his house at the end of his life after becoming paralysed, and there he wrote his most important books: al-Nihaya fi Gharib al-Hadith wa al-Athar and Jami al-Usul fi Ahadith al-Rasul, both of which remain essential references for students of hadith. Ibn Kathir and Ibn Khallikan mentioned that his death was on Thursday, the last day of Dhu al-Hijjah.

sources: الذهبي، تذكرة الحفاظ، الطبقة التاسعة، ترجمة أبي زرعة: (مات أبو زرعة في آخر يوم من سنة أربع وستين ومائتين) — https://ar.wikisource.org/wiki/تذكرة_الحفاظ/الطبقة_التاسعة

en.title: Death of Imam Abu Zur'a al-Razi, master of the hadith scholars of his era
en.body: On the last day of the year 264 AH, Imam Abu Zur'a Ubaydullah ibn Abd al-Karim al-Razi passed away in the city of Rayy, one of the eminent scholars and critics of Prophetic hadith. He travelled in pursuit of knowledge to the Hijaz, the Levant, Egypt, Iraq and Khurasan, and was proverbial in memorization and knowledge of hidden defects and narrators, along with asceticism and humility; Imam Muslim would present some of his hadith to him. Al-Dhahabi stated that he died on the last day of that year, and Ibn Kathir said that his death was on Monday, the last day of Dhu al-Hijjah.
